docs.title: shape validate
docs.text:
Stability: stable.

usage: shape validate [-h] [--json] FILE

Validate FILE: a Shape generation schema goes through the schema validator, a contract through the
contract validation; any other document exits 2.

positional arguments:
  FILE

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      print exactly one JSON document on standard output (format shape-result; the text
              goes to standard error)

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  1   the schema or contract structure is not valid
  2   an unknown contract rule or malformed rule value, or bad input:
      a missing or unreadable file, the wrong kind of file, or a bad
      argument

docs.title: shape verify
docs.text:
Stability: stable.

usage: shape verify [-h] [--key PUBLIC.pub] [--format {auto,csv,parquet,jsonl}]
                    [--schema GATES.json] [--config CONFIG.json] [--source DATA] [--statistical]
                    [-o REPORT] [--strict] [--junit FILE] [--sarif FILE] [--notify REF]
                    [--project FILE] [--no-project] [--changes FILE] [--no-changes]
                    [--on YYYY-MM-DD] [--json] [--dry-run]
                    DATA|ARTIFACT.shape

positional arguments:
  DATA|ARTIFACT.shape   a data file or a directory of data files; a .shape file is checked for its
                        signature instead (exit 1 if invalid)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --key PUBLIC.pub      public key for a .shape artifact
  --format {auto,csv,parquet,jsonl}
  --schema GATES.json   gate schema (or Shape model v2)
  --config CONFIG.json  verify configuration (format shape-verify-config): ranges, date_range,
                        no_future, ordering, baseline, file_paths; runs the range, temporal, drift
                        and file gates
  --source DATA         the real data the generated data was made from (same layout as DATA, same
                        --format): runs the memorization gate, and the utility gate when the
                        configuration has a utility section
  --statistical         add KS and chi-squared tests
  -o REPORT, --output REPORT
                        write a .json or .md report
  --strict              exit 1 on warnings too
  --notify REF          also send the result to this webhook (an env:// or file:// reference to
                        its address; repeatable), on top of the notifications of shape.yml
  --json                print exactly one JSON document on standard output (format shape-result;
                        the text goes to standard error)
  --dry-run             read and check the inputs and print what the command would write or send,
                        then exit 0 (2 for invalid input); nothing is written and no connection is
                        opened

CI reports (defaults: the `ci:` block of shape.yml):
  --junit FILE          write the checks as JUnit XML
  --sarif FILE          write the findings as SARIF 2.1.0

project file (shape.yml):
  --project FILE        use this project file instead of searching
  --no-project          ignore shape.yml

planned changes (shape-changes.yml):
  --changes FILE        the planned-change file (default: the `changes` key of shape.yml, else
                        shape-changes.yml next to it); see docs/PLANNED_CHANGES.md
  --no-changes          ignore planned changes
  --on YYYY-MM-DD       the date planned changes are active on (default: today, UTC)

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  1   a validation gate failed that is enforced (a warning too with
      `--strict`), or the `.shape` file's signature is invalid
  2   bad input: a missing or unreadable file, the wrong kind of file,
      or a bad argument

docs.title: shape quality
docs.text:
Stability: experimental.

usage: shape quality [-h] [--reference CAPTURE.json] [--json] DATA

(experimental)

positional arguments:
  DATA                  a CSV, Parquet or JSONL file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --reference CAPTURE.json
                        the capture the rules come from (default: a capture of DATA itself)
  --json                print exactly one JSON document on standard output (format shape-result;
                        the text goes to standard error)

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  2   a rule was violated, or bad input: a missing or unreadable file,
      the wrong kind of file, or a bad argument

docs.title: shape generate
docs.text:
Stability: stable.

usage: shape generate [-h] [--mode {3nf,star}] [--scale PRESET] [--seed SEED]
                      [--identifiers {reserved,realistic}] [--format FORMAT] [-o DIR] [--dry-run]
                      [--json] [--chunk-rows N]
                      [--sql-dialect {tsql,tsql-fabric-warehouse,postgres,mysql}]
                      [--schema-name NAME] [--batch-size N] [--sql-ddl | --no-sql-ddl]
                      [--sql-drop | --no-sql-drop] [--sql-go | --no-sql-go] [--chaos-log FILE]
                      [--drift-plan FILE] [--delta-mode {overwrite,append}]
                      [--partition-by COLUMN] [--path-template TEMPLATE] [--batch-date YYYY-MM-DD]
                      [--table-format TABLE=FORMAT] [--to URI] [--roll-rows N] [--roll-seconds S]
                      [--commit-rows N]
                      [--write-mode {overwrite,append,fail,create,truncate,replace,upsert}]
                      [--sql-constraints {keep,disable}] [--manifest] [--yes] [--from X.shape]
                      [--decisions DECISIONS.json] [--mixed-copula] [--vault VAULT] [--kek REF]
                      [--verify PUBKEY] [--rows N|TABLE=N]
                      [--scale-mode {local_single,local_mp,fabric_spark}] [--sink NAME]
                      [--sink-config SINK.KEY=VALUE] [--chunk-size N] [--max-workers N]
                      [--processes N] [--fabric-workspace GUID] [--fabric-lakehouse GUID]
                      [--lakehouse-schema NAME] [--fabric-notebook NAME] [--table-prefix P]
                      [--jobs-dir DIR] [--auth {cli,msi,spn,sql,device-code,fabric,kerberos}]
                      [--tenant-id GUID] [--client-id GUID] [--client-secret REF]
                      [--sql-user NAME] [--sql-password REF] [--keytab REF]
                      [--principal NAME@REALM] [--connection-string STR|REF] [--fingerprint]
                      [DOMAIN|SCHEMA.json]

Generate every table of a domain (or of a generation schema file) and write it in the chosen
format. `--dry-run` plans the run and generates nothing. With no target, `--rows N` prints N demo
rows as JSON lines (not from any schema). `--rows TABLE=N` (repeatable) sets the row count of one
table of a schema.

positional arguments:
  DOMAIN|SCHEMA.json    an installed domain (see `shape list`) or a generation schema file (`shape
                        from-ddl` writes one)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --mode {3nf,star}     the schema mode of a domain (default: its own default)
  --scale PRESET        the scale preset (see `shape presets`)
  --seed SEED           the seed (default: the schema's)
  --identifiers {reserved,realistic}
                        reserved: e-mail, URI, phone and SSN values that cannot belong to a real
                        person; realistic: values that can (never for data that leaves a test
                        system). Default: the schema's `identifiers`, else reserved; a column's
                        own `domains` or `range` wins
  --format FORMAT, -f FORMAT
                        summary (default: print the plan result, write nothing), or csv, tsv,
                        jsonl, parquet, ipc, excel, sql, delta, or any installed sink (see `shape
                        plugins list`)
  -o DIR, --output DIR, --out DIR
                        the output directory (needed to write)
  --dry-run             plan the run; generate nothing
  --json                print the result or the plan as JSON
  --chunk-rows N        rows per chunk (output does not depend on it)
  --from X.shape        generate from a profile (a .shape file, or dataset:NAME for one of the
                        dataset library): fits strategies to it
  --decisions DECISIONS.json
                        with --from: apply a decision file (`shape proposals`)
  --mixed-copula        with --from: link the numeric and categorical columns by the profile's
                        mixed-type Gaussian copula (`joint.copula`); every column keeps its
                        generated values (off: the output is unchanged)
  --vault VAULT         with --from: shape plus vault, categories and bounds from a value vault
                        (needs --kek); the output contains real values, treat it like the source
                        data
  --kek REF             with --vault: the key-encryption key, env://NAME or a file
  --verify PUBKEY       with --from: the profile (and the vault hash it records) must carry a
                        valid signature by this public key
  --rows N|TABLE=N      TABLE=N (repeatable): rows of one table of the schema; N: with no target,
                        print N demo rows as JSON lines; with --from, the rows of a one-table
                        profile
  --fingerprint         with --format parquet or delta: write the shape.fingerprint
                        footer/property (table_id, run dataset_id, reproducibility tuple); the
                        tables are generated whole first (`shape fingerprint verify` checks it,
                        docs/FINGERPRINT.md)

sql output (--format sql):
  --sql-dialect {tsql,tsql-fabric-warehouse,postgres,mysql}
                        default: tsql
  --schema-name NAME    qualify tables with this schema
  --batch-size N        rows per INSERT (T-SQL: at most 1000)
  --sql-ddl, --no-sql-ddl
                        write CREATE TABLE statements (default: yes)
  --sql-drop, --no-sql-drop
                        write DROP TABLE IF EXISTS statements (default: yes)
  --sql-go, --no-sql-go
                        write GO statements (default: yes)

excel output (--format excel: one workbook, a sheet per table):
  --chaos-log FILE      a chaos ground-truth log (`shape chaos`): the _README sheet lists what it
                        planted
  --drift-plan FILE     a drift plan or its answer key: the _README sheet lists the planted drift

delta output (--format delta):
  --delta-mode {overwrite,append}
  --partition-by COLUMN
                        repeatable

landing layout:
  --path-template TEMPLATE
                        where each table's file goes under -o, e.g.
                        '{table}/ingest_date={date}/{table}_{yyyymmdd}.{ext}' (tokens: {table}
                        {ext} {date} {yyyymmdd} {yyyy} {mm} {dd}); default:
                        {table}/ingest_date={date}/{table}_{yyyymmdd}.{ext}
  --batch-date YYYY-MM-DD
                        the business date the date tokens take (never read from the clock)
  --table-format TABLE=FORMAT
                        the format of one table (repeatable); the other tables use --format

targets (--to):
  Write to OneLake / ADLS Gen2 or a database instead of -o DIR. Examples: --to
  abfss://landing@acct.dfs.core.windows.net/raw --to
  delta+abfss://ws@onelake.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com/lh.Lakehouse/Tables --to mssql://host/db
  --to postgresql://host/db. Files use --format (default parquet), --path-template, --batch-date
  and --table-format.

  --to URI              a target URI (repeatable: every target gets every table)
  --roll-rows N         files: start a new file every N rows
  --roll-seconds S      files: start a new file every S seconds
  --commit-rows N       Delta and databases: commit every N rows, so readers see rows during the
                        run
  --write-mode {overwrite,append,fail,create,truncate,replace,upsert}
                        what to do with data already there (files: overwrite, append or fail;
                        databases: create (the default; never touches an existing table), append,
                        truncate or replace; mssql:// also upsert: merge on the primary key, so a
                        rerun leaves the same rows)
  --sql-constraints {keep,disable}
                        mssql:// targets: keep (the default) or disable the foreign key and check
                        constraints of tables that already exist while loading, then validate them
                        (exit 1 and the constraints named when one does not hold)
  --manifest            files: write a _SUCCESS file in each folder after its files
  --yes                 confirm writing to a non-local target (not a path, file://, console,
                        localhost); SHAPE_CONFIRM_REMOTE=1 does the same for scripts and notebooks

scale (--scale-mode):
  --scale-mode {local_single,local_mp,fabric_spark}
                        generate through the scale router: local_single (one thread), local_mp
                        (every core) or fabric_spark (a Fabric Spark notebook run); output goes to
                        --sink
  --sink NAME           where the chunks go (memory, parquet, lakehouse, warehouse, sql_database,
                        kql); repeatable. Default: parquet in -o DIR, else memory
  --sink-config SINK.KEY=VALUE
                        a setting of a sink, for example lakehouse.base_path=abfss://...;
                        repeatable
  --chunk-size N        rows per chunk and per part file (500000)
  --max-workers N       generation threads (default: all)
  --processes N         make the Parquet part files in N worker processes (parquet sink alone;
                        schemas with no post-pass)
  --fabric-workspace GUID
                        fabric_spark: the workspace id
  --fabric-lakehouse GUID
                        fabric_spark: the Lakehouse id
  --lakehouse-schema NAME
                        fabric_spark: the schema of a schema-enabled Lakehouse (default dbo; the
                        Lakehouse kind is looked up in Fabric; an error for a classic Lakehouse)
  --fabric-notebook NAME
                        fabric_spark: the worker notebook (default shape_spark_worker; created if
                        absent)
  --table-prefix P      prefix of the physical destination tables (Delta, database and Fabric
                        sinks)
  --jobs-dir DIR        the job store (default: $SHAPE_JOBS_DIR or ~/.shape/jobs)

authentication:
  --auth {cli,msi,spn,sql,device-code,fabric,kerberos}
                        how to sign in to Fabric / Azure: cli (az login, the default), msi
                        (managed identity), spn (service principal), sql (SQL login), device-code
                        (browser sign-in) or fabric (the Fabric notebook identity) or kerberos (a
                        keytab, for a SQL Server that takes Windows authentication only)
  --tenant-id GUID      Entra tenant (spn, device-code)
  --client-id GUID      Entra application (spn, device-code, msi)
  --client-secret REF   spn: the application secret, a credential reference: env://NAME,
                        file://PATH or kv://VAULT/SECRET
  --sql-user NAME       sql: the login name
  --sql-password REF    sql: the login's password, a credential reference: env://NAME, file://PATH
                        or kv://VAULT/SECRET
  --keytab REF          kerberos: the keytab, file://PATH (mode 600) or kv://VAULT/NAME (the
                        keytab base64-encoded); Shape runs kinit into a private cache that is
                        removed when the command ends
  --principal NAME@REALM
                        kerberos: the service principal
  --connection-string STR|REF
                        the ODBC connection string of a SQL destination (server and database; no
                        password), or a credential reference: env://NAME, file://PATH or
                        kv://VAULT/SECRET

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  1   the plan has problems (`--dry-run`), or a sink or the scale run
      failed
  2   bad input: a missing or unreadable file, the wrong kind of file,
      or a bad argument
  130 interrupted during a scale run (the job can be resumed)

docs.title: shape composite
docs.text:
Stability: experimental.

usage: shape composite [-h] [--scale PRESET] [--seed SEED] [--identifiers {reserved,realistic}]
                       [--format FORMAT] [-o DIR] [--dry-run] [--json] [--chunk-rows N]
                       [--sql-dialect {tsql,tsql-fabric-warehouse,postgres,mysql}]
                       [--schema-name NAME] [--batch-size N] [--sql-ddl | --no-sql-ddl]
                       [--sql-drop | --no-sql-drop] [--sql-go | --no-sql-go] [--chaos-log FILE]
                       [--drift-plan FILE] [--delta-mode {overwrite,append}]
                       [--partition-by COLUMN] [--path-template TEMPLATE]
                       [--batch-date YYYY-MM-DD] [--table-format TABLE=FORMAT] [--to URI]
                       [--roll-rows N] [--roll-seconds S] [--commit-rows N]
                       [--write-mode {overwrite,append,fail,create,truncate,replace,upsert}]
                       [--sql-constraints {keep,disable}] [--manifest] [--yes]
                       PRESET|DOMAIN+DOMAIN

(experimental) Generate a composite: the domains of a preset (see `shape presets --composites`) or
domains joined by '+' (retail+hr+financial), merged into one dataset whose tables are prefixed
with their domain (retail_customer). Shared entities (a person, a location, an organisation) link
the domains by bridge columns.

positional arguments:
  PRESET|DOMAIN+DOMAIN  a composite preset or domains

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --scale PRESET        the scale preset (see `shape presets`)
  --seed SEED           the seed (default: the schema's)
  --identifiers {reserved,realistic}
                        reserved: e-mail, URI, phone and SSN values that cannot belong to a real
                        person; realistic: values that can (never for data that leaves a test
                        system). Default: the schema's `identifiers`, else reserved; a column's
                        own `domains` or `range` wins
  --format FORMAT, -f FORMAT
                        summary (default: print the plan result, write nothing), or csv, tsv,
                        jsonl, parquet, ipc, excel, sql, delta, or any installed sink (see `shape
                        plugins list`)
  -o DIR, --output DIR, --out DIR
                        the output directory (needed to write)
  --dry-run             plan the run; generate nothing
  --json                print the result or the plan as JSON
  --chunk-rows N        rows per chunk (output does not depend on it)

sql output (--format sql):
  --sql-dialect {tsql,tsql-fabric-warehouse,postgres,mysql}
                        default: tsql
  --schema-name NAME    qualify tables with this schema
  --batch-size N        rows per INSERT (T-SQL: at most 1000)
  --sql-ddl, --no-sql-ddl
                        write CREATE TABLE statements (default: yes)
  --sql-drop, --no-sql-drop
                        write DROP TABLE IF EXISTS statements (default: yes)
  --sql-go, --no-sql-go
                        write GO statements (default: yes)

excel output (--format excel: one workbook, a sheet per table):
  --chaos-log FILE      a chaos ground-truth log (`shape chaos`): the _README sheet lists what it
                        planted
  --drift-plan FILE     a drift plan or its answer key: the _README sheet lists the planted drift

delta output (--format delta):
  --delta-mode {overwrite,append}
  --partition-by COLUMN
                        repeatable

landing layout:
  --path-template TEMPLATE
                        where each table's file goes under -o, e.g.
                        '{table}/ingest_date={date}/{table}_{yyyymmdd}.{ext}' (tokens: {table}
                        {ext} {date} {yyyymmdd} {yyyy} {mm} {dd}); default:
                        {table}/ingest_date={date}/{table}_{yyyymmdd}.{ext}
  --batch-date YYYY-MM-DD
                        the business date the date tokens take (never read from the clock)
  --table-format TABLE=FORMAT
                        the format of one table (repeatable); the other tables use --format

targets (--to):
  Write to OneLake / ADLS Gen2 or a database instead of -o DIR. Examples: --to
  abfss://landing@acct.dfs.core.windows.net/raw --to
  delta+abfss://ws@onelake.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com/lh.Lakehouse/Tables --to mssql://host/db
  --to postgresql://host/db. Files use --format (default parquet), --path-template, --batch-date
  and --table-format.

  --to URI              a target URI (repeatable: every target gets every table)
  --roll-rows N         files: start a new file every N rows
  --roll-seconds S      files: start a new file every S seconds
  --commit-rows N       Delta and databases: commit every N rows, so readers see rows during the
                        run
  --write-mode {overwrite,append,fail,create,truncate,replace,upsert}
                        what to do with data already there (files: overwrite, append or fail;
                        databases: create (the default; never touches an existing table), append,
                        truncate or replace; mssql:// also upsert: merge on the primary key, so a
                        rerun leaves the same rows)
  --sql-constraints {keep,disable}
                        mssql:// targets: keep (the default) or disable the foreign key and check
                        constraints of tables that already exist while loading, then validate them
                        (exit 1 and the constraints named when one does not hold)
  --manifest            files: write a _SUCCESS file in each folder after its files
  --yes                 confirm writing to a non-local target (not a path, file://, console,
                        localhost); SHAPE_CONFIRM_REMOTE=1 does the same for scripts and notebooks

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  1   a sink or the scale run failed, or constraints did not hold
      after `--sql-constraints disable` loaded the rows
  2   bad input: a missing or unreadable file, the wrong kind of file,
      or a bad argument
  130 interrupted during a scale run (the job can be resumed)

docs.title: shape emit
docs.text:
Stability: experimental.

usage: shape emit [-h] [--key KEY] [--header HEADER] [--partition PARTITION]
                  [--partition-key PARTITION_KEY] [--timestamp {broker,event_time}]
                  [--mode {3nf,star}] [--scale PRESET] [--seed SEED] [--table NAME] [--sink SINK]
                  [--auth {cli,msi,spn,sql,device-code,fabric,kerberos}] [--tenant-id GUID]
                  [--client-id GUID] [--client-secret REF] [--sql-user NAME] [--sql-password REF]
                  [--keytab REF] [--principal NAME@REALM] [--connection-string STR|REF] [-o FILE]
                  [--envelope {flat,cloudevents}]
                  [--event-format {json,avro,protobuf,json-schema}] [--realtime | --no-realtime]
                  [--rate N] [--burst START:DURATION:MULT] [--ramp START:DURATION:FROM:TO]
                  [--daily-curve NAME|FILE] [--arrivals {constant,poisson}] [--max-rate N]
                  [--speed FACTOR] [--max-events N] [--duration SECONDS] [--drift-plan PLAN.json]
                  [--rows TABLE=N] [--day-seconds S] [--out-of-order F] [--ooo-window N]
                  [--anomaly-fraction F] [--anomaly-mutator NAME] [--duplicate-fraction F]
                  [--duplicate-window N] [--poison-fraction F] [--answer-key FILE]
                  [--synthetic-header | --no-synthetic-header] [--path-template TEMPLATE]
                  [--batch-date YYYY-MM-DD] [--table-format TABLE=FORMAT] [--to URI]
                  [--format {parquet,csv,tsv,jsonl,ipc}] [--roll-rows N] [--roll-seconds S]
                  [--commit-rows N]
                  [--write-mode {overwrite,append,fail,create,truncate,replace,upsert}]
                  [--sql-constraints {keep,disable}] [--sink-config SINK.KEY=VALUE] [--manifest]
                  [--yes] [--checkpoint FILE] [--checkpoint-every N] [--checkpoint-seconds S]
                  [--dead-letter URI] [--max-dead-letter N] [--fresh] [--batch-events N]
                  [--queue-batches N] [--retries N] [--dry-run] [--progress | --no-progress]
                  [--json] [--live-target DOMAIN|SCHEMA.json|PATH] [--live-target-seed N]
                  [--live-target-scale PRESET] [--live-alerts FILE] [--live-report FILE]
                  [--live-profile FILE] [--live-min-score N] [--live-min-table-score N]
                  [--live-min-column-score N] [--live-drop POINTS] [--live-min-events N]
                  [--live-min-progress F] [--live-interval N] [--live-interval-seconds S]
                  [--live-sample N] [--live-key-cap N] [--no-live-profile] [--live-fail]
                  DOMAIN|SCHEMA.json

(experimental) Emit the rows of a domain (or of a generation schema file) as JSON-lines events: as
fast as possible (the default) or paced in real time with --realtime. Each event is the row plus
_shape_table, _shape_seq and (when the table has a date or timestamp column) _shape_event_time;
(_shape_table, _shape_seq) is the idempotency key. Delivery is at-least-once: after a crash, run
the same command again to resume.

positional arguments:
  DOMAIN|SCHEMA.json    an installed domain or a schema

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --key KEY             broker key: column or columns joined by | (default idempotency)
  --header HEADER       broker header name=value or name=@column
  --partition PARTITION
                        Kafka partition number or by_key
  --partition-key PARTITION_KEY
                        Event Hubs table, none or column
  --timestamp {broker,event_time}
                        broker time or event time
  --mode {3nf,star}     the schema mode of a domain
  --scale PRESET        the scale preset (see `shape presets`)
  --seed SEED           the seed (default: the schema's)
  --table NAME          stream only this table (repeatable)
  --sink SINK           console (events on standard output, the default), file (JSON lines in
                        --output), or the URI of an emitter: file:///PATH, jsonl:///DIR, kafka://,
                        eventhubs://, eventstream://, eventhouse:// (the last four come with their
                        plugins)
  -o FILE, --output FILE
                        the file for --sink file
  --envelope {flat,cloudevents}
                        flat rows (default) or CloudEvents 1.0 structured JSON
  --event-format {json,avro,protobuf,json-schema}
                        the message format of a kafka:// target: json (default: the flat event's
                        JSON), or avro, protobuf or json-schema through a schema registry (--sink-
                        config kafka.schema_registry_url=URL; see docs/EMIT.md)
  --dry-run             resolve everything the run would use (target, tables, destinations and
                        their plugins, checkpoint state, rate schedule, drift plan) and print it,
                        opening no connection, writing no file and sending no event; exit 2 when
                        the run would be refused
  --progress, --no-progress
                        one progress line on standard error, rewritten once a second (default: on
                        when standard error is a terminal)
  --json                print the run report as JSON (with --dry-run: the plan, format shape-emit-
                        plan)

authentication:
  --auth {cli,msi,spn,sql,device-code,fabric,kerberos}
                        how to sign in to Fabric / Azure: cli (az login, the default), msi
                        (managed identity), spn (service principal), sql (SQL login), device-code
                        (browser sign-in) or fabric (the Fabric notebook identity) or kerberos (a
                        keytab, for a SQL Server that takes Windows authentication only)
  --tenant-id GUID      Entra tenant (spn, device-code)
  --client-id GUID      Entra application (spn, device-code, msi)
  --client-secret REF   spn: the application secret, a credential reference: env://NAME,
                        file://PATH or kv://VAULT/SECRET
  --sql-user NAME       sql: the login name
  --sql-password REF    sql: the login's password, a credential reference: env://NAME, file://PATH
                        or kv://VAULT/SECRET
  --keytab REF          kerberos: the keytab, file://PATH (mode 600) or kv://VAULT/NAME (the
                        keytab base64-encoded); Shape runs kinit into a private cache that is
                        removed when the command ends
  --principal NAME@REALM
                        kerberos: the service principal
  --connection-string STR|REF
                        the ODBC connection string of a SQL destination (server and database; no
                        password), or a credential reference: env://NAME, file://PATH or
                        kv://VAULT/SECRET

rate:
  --realtime, --no-realtime
                        pace to --rate events per second (default: --no-realtime, as fast as
                        possible)
  --rate N              events/s (100)
  --burst START:DURATION:MULT
                        from START seconds for DURATION seconds the rate is MULT times --rate
                        (repeatable)
  --ramp START:DURATION:FROM:TO
                        from START seconds for DURATION seconds the rate multiplier moves linearly
                        from FROM to TO, and holds TO after (repeatable; ramps may not overlap;
                        needs --realtime)
  --daily-curve NAME|FILE
                        a 24-hour rate multiplier: flat, business-hours, or a shape-rate-curve
                        JSON file; follows the wall clock with --realtime and the event time with
                        --speed
  --arrivals {constant,poisson}
                        events evenly spaced (default) or with random exponential gaps of mean
                        1/rate (poisson; a function of the seed and the event position, the same
                        on every run and after a resume); needs --realtime
  --max-rate N          a hard cap: never more than N events per second, whatever else is set
  --speed FACTOR        replay by event time, FACTOR times the clock rate (60x: an hour in a
                        minute); needs events with a date or timestamp column, in time order
                        (`shape stream`)
  --max-events N        stop after N events in all
  --duration SECONDS    stop after SECONDS

drift plan:
  Plant the drift of a `shape generate-drift` plan in the stream, day by day (docs/EMIT.md,
  'Drift plans in a stream').

  --drift-plan PLAN.json
                        emit the plan's days in order: day d is generated from the plan's schema
                        for d with seed + d, as `shape generate-drift` does; _shape_seq continues
                        across days
  --rows TABLE=N        rows per day for one table, as in `shape generate-drift` (repeatable;
                        needs --drift-plan)
  --day-seconds S       with --realtime: each day of the plan takes S seconds, its events spread
                        evenly (replaces --rate, --burst, --ramp, --daily-curve and --arrivals)

event shape:
  --out-of-order F      fraction of events delivered late (0-1, default 0)
  --ooo-window N        a late event moves at most N places later (default 1000)
  --anomaly-fraction F  fraction of events whose values are mutated (0-1, default 0)
  --anomaly-mutator NAME
                        a shape.chaos mutator to apply to them (repeatable; default: value-
                        anomaly)

faults and the answer key:
  Injected on top of --out-of-order and --anomaly-fraction; the same events every run.

  --duplicate-fraction F
                        fraction of events delivered a second time later (at-least-once delivery)
  --duplicate-window N  a copy arrives 1 to N events later (default 1000)
  --poison-fraction F   fraction of events delivered cut off, as invalid JSON (file, console,
                        Kafka, Event Hubs)
  --answer-key FILE     write every injected fault (late, anomaly, duplicate, poison) to FILE as
                        JSON lines
  --synthetic-header, --no-synthetic-header
                        mark every message of a transport that has headers (Kafka, Event Hubs,
                        Eventstream) as synthetic: header shape-synthetic (default: on)

landing layout:
  --path-template TEMPLATE
                        where each table's file goes under -o, e.g.
                        '{table}/ingest_date={date}/{table}_{yyyymmdd}.{ext}' (tokens: {table}
                        {ext} {date} {yyyymmdd} {yyyy} {mm} {dd})
  --batch-date YYYY-MM-DD
                        the business date the date tokens take (never read from the clock)
  --table-format TABLE=FORMAT
                        the format of one table (repeatable); the other tables use --format

targets (--to):
  Write to OneLake / ADLS Gen2 or a database instead of -o DIR. Examples: --to
  abfss://landing@acct.dfs.core.windows.net/raw --to
  delta+abfss://ws@onelake.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com/lh.Lakehouse/Tables --to mssql://host/db
  --to postgresql://host/db. Files use --format (default parquet), --path-template, --batch-date
  and --table-format.

  --to URI              a target URI (repeatable: every target gets every table)
  --format {parquet,csv,tsv,jsonl,ipc}, -f {parquet,csv,tsv,jsonl,ipc}
                        the file format of abfss:// targets (default parquet)
  --roll-rows N         files: start a new file every N rows
  --roll-seconds S      files: start a new file every S seconds
  --commit-rows N       Delta and databases: commit every N rows, so readers see rows during the
                        run
  --write-mode {overwrite,append,fail,create,truncate,replace,upsert}
                        what to do with data already there (files: overwrite, append or fail;
                        databases: create (the default; never touches an existing table), append,
                        truncate or replace; mssql:// also upsert: merge on the primary key, so a
                        rerun leaves the same rows)
  --sql-constraints {keep,disable}
                        mssql:// targets: keep (the default) or disable the foreign key and check
                        constraints of tables that already exist while loading, then validate them
                        (exit 1 and the constraints named when one does not hold)
  --sink-config SINK.KEY=VALUE
                        an option of one sink, e.g. abfss.account_name=acct; a secret must be a
                        reference (env://NAME, file://PATH, kv://VAULT/NAME)
  --manifest            files: write a _SUCCESS file in each folder after its files
  --yes                 confirm writing to a non-local target (not a path, file://, console,
                        localhost); SHAPE_CONFIRM_REMOTE=1 does the same for scripts and notebooks

delivery:
  --checkpoint FILE     checkpoint file (see the description)
  --checkpoint-every N
  --checkpoint-seconds S
                        at least this often (default 1; 30 with a table target, so files are not
                        tiny)
  --dead-letter URI     send an event the destination rejects for good (or that cannot be encoded
                        in --event-format) to this destination, any URI --sink or --to takes,
                        instead of stopping the run (docs/EMIT.md, 'Dead letters')
  --max-dead-letter N   stop the run (exit 1) once more than N events were dead-lettered
  --fresh               ignore an existing checkpoint
  --batch-events N      events per delivery
  --queue-batches N     buffer depth
  --retries N           per failed delivery

live fidelity:
  Score the emitted events against a target as they go (docs/EMIT.md, 'Live fidelity'). The
  score is the one `shape fidelity` gives; the stream profiler sees every event.

  --live-target DOMAIN|SCHEMA.json|PATH
                        what the stream is compared with: a domain or schema (the reference is
                        generated from it with --live-target-seed) or reference data (a file or
                        directory of one file per table, as `shape fidelity` reads it). Turns live
                        fidelity on
  --live-target-seed N  the seed of a generated reference (default: the stream's seed plus 1)
  --live-target-scale PRESET
                        the scale of a generated reference
  --live-alerts FILE    append every alert to FILE as JSON lines (alerts always go to standard
                        error)
  --live-report FILE    write the final live report: .json (summary, alerts, trajectory, report),
                        .md, .html
  --live-profile FILE   write the live stream profile (JSON, per table)
  --live-min-score N    overall pass mark (85)
  --live-min-table-score N
                        table pass mark (70)
  --live-min-column-score N
                        alert on a column below N (default: columns are not judged)
  --live-drop POINTS    alert when a table's score falls POINTS below its best (5)
  --live-min-events N   events of a table before the alerts judge it (1000)
  --live-min-progress F
                        share of a target table's rows to see before the alerts judge it (0.5)
  --live-interval N     score after every N events (50000) and at least --live-interval-seconds
                        apart
  --live-interval-seconds S
                        (2 seconds)
  --live-sample N       values kept per numeric column for the KS statistic (100000)
  --live-key-cap N      distinct values tracked per column before the profiler's sketches take
                        over
  --no-live-profile     do not feed the stream profiler (faster; --live-profile is then
                        unavailable)
  --live-fail           exit 1 when an error alert was raised or the final score misses a pass
                        mark

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  1   a live target failed (with `--live-fail`)
  2   bad input: a missing or unreadable file, the wrong kind of file,
      or a bad argument

docs.text:
Stability: experimental.

usage: shape stream [-h] [--key KEY] [--header HEADER] [--partition PARTITION]
                    [--partition-key PARTITION_KEY] [--timestamp {broker,event_time}]
                    [--mode {3nf,star}] [--scale PRESET] [--seed SEED] --table NAME [--sink SINK]
                    [--auth {cli,msi,spn,sql,device-code,fabric,kerberos}] [--tenant-id GUID]
                    [--client-id GUID] [--client-secret REF] [--sql-user NAME]

                    [--connection-string STR|REF] [-o FILE] [--envelope {flat,cloudevents}]
                    [--event-format {json,avro,protobuf,json-schema}] [--realtime | --no-realtime]
                    [--rate N] [--burst START:DURATION:MULT] [--ramp START:DURATION:FROM:TO]
                    [--daily-curve NAME|FILE] [--arrivals {constant,poisson}] [--max-rate N]
                    [--speed FACTOR] [--max-events N] [--duration SECONDS]
                    [--drift-plan PLAN.json] [--rows TABLE=N] [--day-seconds S] [--out-of-order F]
                    [--ooo-window N] [--anomaly-fraction F] [--anomaly-mutator NAME]
                    [--duplicate-fraction F] [--duplicate-window N] [--poison-fraction F]
                    [--answer-key FILE] [--synthetic-header | --no-synthetic-header]
                    [--path-template TEMPLATE] [--batch-date YYYY-MM-DD]
                    [--table-format TABLE=FORMAT] [--to URI]
                    [--format {parquet,csv,tsv,jsonl,ipc}] [--roll-rows N] [--roll-seconds S]
                    [--commit-rows N]
                    [--write-mode {overwrite,append,fail,create,truncate,replace,upsert}]
                    [--sql-constraints {keep,disable}] [--sink-config SINK.KEY=VALUE] [--manifest]
                    [--yes] [--checkpoint FILE] [--checkpoint-every N] [--checkpoint-seconds S]
                    [--dead-letter URI] [--max-dead-letter N] [--fresh] [--batch-events N]
                    [--queue-batches N] [--retries N] [--dry-run] [--progress | --no-progress]
                    [--json] [--live-target DOMAIN|SCHEMA.json|PATH] [--live-target-seed N]
                    [--live-target-scale PRESET] [--live-alerts FILE] [--live-report FILE]
                    [--live-profile FILE] [--live-min-score N] [--live-min-table-score N]
                    [--live-min-column-score N] [--live-drop POINTS] [--live-min-events N]
                    [--live-min-progress F] [--live-interval N] [--live-interval-seconds S]
                    [--live-sample N] [--live-key-cap N] [--no-live-profile] [--live-fail]

(experimental) Stream one table of a domain (or of a generation schema file) as JSON-lines events,
earliest event first: as fast as possible (the default) or paced in real time with --realtime.
Each event is the row plus _shape_table, _shape_seq and (when the table has a date or timestamp
column) _shape_event_time; (_shape_table, _shape_seq) is the idempotency key. Same runtime as
`shape emit` (see docs/EMIT.md), which streams several tables in dependency order instead.

positional arguments:
  DOMAIN|SCHEMA.json    an installed domain or a schema

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --key KEY             broker key: column or columns joined by | (default idempotency)
  --header HEADER       broker header name=value or name=@column
  --partition PARTITION
                        Kafka partition number or by_key
  --partition-key PARTITION_KEY
                        Event Hubs table, none or column
  --timestamp {broker,event_time}
                        broker time or event time
  --mode {3nf,star}, -m {3nf,star}
                        the schema mode of a domain
  --scale PRESET, -s PRESET
                        the scale preset (see `shape presets`)
  --seed SEED           the seed (default: the schema's)
  --table NAME, -t NAME
                        the table to stream (required)
  --sink SINK           console (events on standard output, the default), file (JSON lines in
                        --output), or the URI of an emitter: file:///PATH, jsonl:///DIR, kafka://,
                        eventhubs://, eventstream://, eventhouse:// (the last four come with their
                        plugins)
  -o FILE, --output FILE
                        the file for --sink file
  --envelope {flat,cloudevents}
                        flat rows (default) or CloudEvents 1.0 structured JSON
  --event-format {json,avro,protobuf,json-schema}
                        the message format of a kafka:// target: json (default: the flat event's
                        JSON), or avro, protobuf or json-schema through a schema registry (--sink-
                        config kafka.schema_registry_url=URL; see docs/EMIT.md)
  --dry-run             resolve everything the run would use (target, tables, destinations and
                        their plugins, checkpoint state, rate schedule, drift plan) and print it,
                        opening no connection, writing no file and sending no event; exit 2 when
                        the run would be refused
  --progress, --no-progress
                        one progress line on standard error, rewritten once a second (default: on
                        when standard error is a terminal)
  --json                print the run report as JSON (with --dry-run: the plan, format shape-emit-
                        plan)

authentication:
  --auth {cli,msi,spn,sql,device-code,fabric,kerberos}
                        how to sign in to Fabric / Azure: cli (az login, the default), msi
                        (managed identity), spn (service principal), sql (SQL login), device-code
                        (browser sign-in) or fabric (the Fabric notebook identity) or kerberos (a
                        keytab, for a SQL Server that takes Windows authentication only)
  --tenant-id GUID      Entra tenant (spn, device-code)
  --client-id GUID      Entra application (spn, device-code, msi)
  --client-secret REF   spn: the application secret, a credential reference: env://NAME,
                        file://PATH or kv://VAULT/SECRET
  --sql-user NAME       sql: the login name
  --sql-password REF    sql: the login's password, a credential reference: env://NAME, file://PATH
                        or kv://VAULT/SECRET
  --keytab REF          kerberos: the keytab, file://PATH (mode 600) or kv://VAULT/NAME (the
                        keytab base64-encoded); Shape runs kinit into a private cache that is
                        removed when the command ends
  --principal NAME@REALM
                        kerberos: the service principal
  --connection-string STR|REF
                        the ODBC connection string of a SQL destination (server and database; no
                        password), or a credential reference: env://NAME, file://PATH or
                        kv://VAULT/SECRET

rate:
  --realtime, --no-realtime
                        pace to --rate events per second (default: --no-realtime, as fast as
                        possible)
  --rate N              events/s (10)
  --burst START:DURATION:MULT
                        from START seconds for DURATION seconds the rate is MULT times --rate
                        (repeatable)
  --ramp START:DURATION:FROM:TO
                        from START seconds for DURATION seconds the rate multiplier moves linearly
                        from FROM to TO, and holds TO after (repeatable; ramps may not overlap;
                        needs --realtime)
  --daily-curve NAME|FILE
                        a 24-hour rate multiplier: flat, business-hours, or a shape-rate-curve
                        JSON file; follows the wall clock with --realtime and the event time with
                        --speed
  --arrivals {constant,poisson}
                        events evenly spaced (default) or with random exponential gaps of mean
                        1/rate (poisson; a function of the seed and the event position, the same
                        on every run and after a resume); needs --realtime
  --max-rate N          a hard cap: never more than N events per second, whatever else is set
  --speed FACTOR        replay by event time, FACTOR times the clock rate (60x: an hour in a
                        minute); needs events with a date or timestamp column, in time order
                        (`shape stream`)
  --max-events N        stop after N events in all
  --duration SECONDS    stop after SECONDS

drift plan:
  Plant the drift of a `shape generate-drift` plan in the stream, day by day (docs/EMIT.md,
  'Drift plans in a stream').

  --drift-plan PLAN.json
                        emit the plan's days in order: day d is generated from the plan's schema
                        for d with seed + d, as `shape generate-drift` does; _shape_seq continues
                        across days
  --rows TABLE=N        rows per day for one table, as in `shape generate-drift` (repeatable;
                        needs --drift-plan)
  --day-seconds S       with --realtime: each day of the plan takes S seconds, its events spread
                        evenly (replaces --rate, --burst, --ramp, --daily-curve and --arrivals)

event shape:
  --out-of-order F      fraction of events delivered late (0-1, default 0)
  --ooo-window N        a late event moves at most N places later (default 1000)
  --anomaly-fraction F  fraction of events whose values are mutated (0-1, default 0)
  --anomaly-mutator NAME
                        a shape.chaos mutator to apply to them (repeatable; default: value-
                        anomaly)

faults and the answer key:
  Injected on top of --out-of-order and --anomaly-fraction; the same events every run.

  --duplicate-fraction F
                        fraction of events delivered a second time later (at-least-once delivery)
  --duplicate-window N  a copy arrives 1 to N events later (default 1000)
  --poison-fraction F   fraction of events delivered cut off, as invalid JSON (file, console,
                        Kafka, Event Hubs)
  --answer-key FILE     write every injected fault (late, anomaly, duplicate, poison) to FILE as
                        JSON lines
  --synthetic-header, --no-synthetic-header
                        mark every message of a transport that has headers (Kafka, Event Hubs,
                        Eventstream) as synthetic: header shape-synthetic (default: on)

landing layout:
  --path-template TEMPLATE
                        where each table's file goes under -o, e.g.
                        '{table}/ingest_date={date}/{table}_{yyyymmdd}.{ext}' (tokens: {table}
                        {ext} {date} {yyyymmdd} {yyyy} {mm} {dd})
  --batch-date YYYY-MM-DD
                        the business date the date tokens take (never read from the clock)
  --table-format TABLE=FORMAT
                        the format of one table (repeatable); the other tables use --format

targets (--to):
  Write to OneLake / ADLS Gen2 or a database instead of -o DIR. Examples: --to
  abfss://landing@acct.dfs.core.windows.net/raw --to
  delta+abfss://ws@onelake.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com/lh.Lakehouse/Tables --to mssql://host/db
  --to postgresql://host/db. Files use --format (default parquet), --path-template, --batch-date
  and --table-format.

  --to URI              a target URI (repeatable: every target gets every table)
  --format {parquet,csv,tsv,jsonl,ipc}, -f {parquet,csv,tsv,jsonl,ipc}
                        the file format of abfss:// targets (default parquet)
  --roll-rows N         files: start a new file every N rows
  --roll-seconds S      files: start a new file every S seconds
  --commit-rows N       Delta and databases: commit every N rows, so readers see rows during the
                        run
  --write-mode {overwrite,append,fail,create,truncate,replace,upsert}
                        what to do with data already there (files: overwrite, append or fail;
                        databases: create (the default; never touches an existing table), append,
                        truncate or replace; mssql:// also upsert: merge on the primary key, so a
                        rerun leaves the same rows)
  --sql-constraints {keep,disable}
                        mssql:// targets: keep (the default) or disable the foreign key and check
                        constraints of tables that already exist while loading, then validate them
                        (exit 1 and the constraints named when one does not hold)
  --sink-config SINK.KEY=VALUE
                        an option of one sink, e.g. abfss.account_name=acct; a secret must be a
                        reference (env://NAME, file://PATH, kv://VAULT/NAME)
  --manifest            files: write a _SUCCESS file in each folder after its files
  --yes                 confirm writing to a non-local target (not a path, file://, console,
                        localhost); SHAPE_CONFIRM_REMOTE=1 does the same for scripts and notebooks

delivery:
  --checkpoint FILE     checkpoint file (see the description)
  --checkpoint-every N
  --checkpoint-seconds S
                        at least this often (default 1; 30 with a table target, so files are not
                        tiny)
  --dead-letter URI     send an event the destination rejects for good (or that cannot be encoded
                        in --event-format) to this destination, any URI --sink or --to takes,
                        instead of stopping the run (docs/EMIT.md, 'Dead letters')
  --max-dead-letter N   stop the run (exit 1) once more than N events were dead-lettered
  --fresh               ignore an existing checkpoint
  --batch-events N      events per delivery
  --queue-batches N     buffer depth
  --retries N           per failed delivery

live fidelity:
  Score the emitted events against a target as they go (docs/EMIT.md, 'Live fidelity'). The
  score is the one `shape fidelity` gives; the stream profiler sees every event.

  --live-target DOMAIN|SCHEMA.json|PATH
                        what the stream is compared with: a domain or schema (the reference is
                        generated from it with --live-target-seed) or reference data (a file or
                        directory of one file per table, as `shape fidelity` reads it). Turns live
                        fidelity on
  --live-target-seed N  the seed of a generated reference (default: the stream's seed plus 1)
  --live-target-scale PRESET
                        the scale of a generated reference
  --live-alerts FILE    append every alert to FILE as JSON lines (alerts always go to standard
                        error)
  --live-report FILE    write the final live report: .json (summary, alerts, trajectory, report),
                        .md, .html
  --live-profile FILE   write the live stream profile (JSON, per table)
  --live-min-score N    overall pass mark (85)
  --live-min-table-score N
                        table pass mark (70)
  --live-min-column-score N
                        alert on a column below N (default: columns are not judged)
  --live-drop POINTS    alert when a table's score falls POINTS below its best (5)
  --live-min-events N   events of a table before the alerts judge it (1000)
  --live-min-progress F
                        share of a target table's rows to see before the alerts judge it (0.5)
  --live-interval N     score after every N events (50000) and at least --live-interval-seconds
                        apart
  --live-interval-seconds S
                        (2 seconds)
  --live-sample N       values kept per numeric column for the KS statistic (100000)
  --live-key-cap N      distinct values tracked per column before the profiler's sketches take
                        over
  --no-live-profile     do not feed the stream profiler (faster; --live-profile is then
                        unavailable)
  --live-fail           exit 1 when an error alert was raised or the final score misses a pass
                        mark

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  1   a live target failed (with `--live-fail`)
  2   bad input: a missing or unreadable file, the wrong kind of file,
      or a bad argument

docs.title: shape mask
docs.text:
Stability: experimental.

usage: shape mask [-h] -o DIR [--format {csv,parquet}] [--seed SEED]
                  [--key-file FILE | --key-env VAR] [--exclude COLUMN] [--pii COLUMN=TYPE]
                  [--json] [--dry-run]
                  PATH

(experimental) Find columns that hold personal data (e-mail, phone, names, addresses, SSN, card
numbers, IP addresses, IBANs, dates of birth, ...) from their names and their values, and replace
them with synthetic values in the same format. Null positions and every other column are kept
exactly; the same original value gets the same replacement everywhere, so keys and the columns
that refer to them still match.

positional arguments:
  PATH                  a data file, or a directory of data files

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -o DIR, --output DIR  directory for the masked files
  --format {csv,parquet}
                        the file format of a directory's files and of the output (default: from
                        the input file's extension; csv for a directory)
  --seed SEED           random seed (default 42)
  --key-file FILE       keyed masking: read the secret key from FILE (not readable by others, and
                        outside the output directory); the same value and key always give the same
                        mask, in any run
  --key-env VAR         keyed masking: read the secret key from this environment variable
  --exclude COLUMN      leave this column as is
  --pii COLUMN=TYPE     mask this column as TYPE even if nothing marks it as personal data
  --json                print the summary as JSON
  --dry-run             read and check the inputs and print what the command would write or send,
                        then exit 0 (2 for invalid input); nothing is written and no connection is
                        opened

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  2   bad input: a missing or unreadable file, the wrong kind of file,
      or a bad argument

docs.title: shape scorecard
docs.text:
Stability: experimental.

usage: shape scorecard [-h] [--format {auto,csv,parquet,jsonl}] [--schema GATES.json]
                       [--config CONFIG.json] [--suppressions FILE.json] [--project FILE]
                       [--no-project] [--source NAME] [--history DIR] [--name NAME] [--record]
                       [--samples N] [--classified TABLE.COLUMN] [--show-classified]
                       [--flag-output DIR] [--flag-column NAME] [--slice-by COLUMN[,COLUMN]]
                       [--min-slice-rows N] [--max-slice-gap G] [--reference REF] [--label COLUMN]
                       [--json] [-o FILE] [--dry-run]
                       DATA

(experimental) Run the validation gates over data and score six dimensions (accuracy,
completeness, conformity, consistency, timeliness, uniqueness) from them, with the owner of each
failing column, the trend over earlier scorecards, and failing-row samples that never show the
values of classified columns unless asked. With --slice-by every dimension is also scored per
slice. Exit 0 when the scorecard was produced (and, with --max-slice-gap, no slice gap is above
it), 1 when a slice gap is above --max-slice-gap, 2 on an input error.

positional arguments:
  DATA                  a data file, or a directory of data files

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --format {auto,csv,parquet,jsonl}
  --schema GATES.json   gate schema (or Shape model v2)
  --config CONFIG.json  verify configuration (see verify)
  --suppressions FILE.json
                        known issues to snooze or suppress (format shape-scorecard-suppressions)
  --history DIR         registry directory holding earlier scorecards
  --name NAME           name of the scorecard series in --history
  --record              add this scorecard to --history
  --samples N           failing rows to show per failing check (default 5; 0 for none)
  --classified TABLE.COLUMN
                        treat this column as classified: samples show [redacted] for it
  --show-classified     show the values of classified columns in samples (off by default)
  --flag-output DIR     write each table, with a boolean flag column marking its failing rows, to
                        DIR
  --flag-column NAME    name of the flag column (default _shape_dq_failed)
  --slice-by COLUMN[,COLUMN]
                        also score every dimension per slice: each value (or value combination) of
                        these columns in the tables that hold them; null is the slice (null)
  --min-slice-rows N    slices with fewer rows are pooled as (small slices) and never shown alone
                        (default 30)
  --max-slice-gap G     exit 1 when any dimension's gap (highest minus lowest slice score) exceeds
                        G
  --reference REF       with --slice-by: data or a profile of the population the data should
                        describe; reports each slice's reference share and the ratio
  --label COLUMN        with --slice-by: a boolean or two-valued column; reports each slice's
                        positive rate and the disparity ratio (flagged below 0.8, the four-fifths
                        screening heuristic)
  --json                print the scorecard as JSON
  -o FILE, --output FILE
                        write the scorecard to FILE
  --dry-run             read and check the inputs and print what the command would write or send,
                        then exit 0 (2 for invalid input); nothing is written and no connection is
                        opened

project file (shape.yml):
  --project FILE        use this project file instead of searching
  --no-project          ignore shape.yml
  --source NAME         the source of shape.yml whose settings apply

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  1   a slice gap is above `--max-slice-gap`
  2   bad input: a missing or unreadable file, the wrong kind of file,
      or a bad argument

docs.title: shape skew
docs.text:
Stability: experimental.

usage: shape skew [-h] [--format {auto,csv,parquet,jsonl}] [--features COLS] [--label COL]
                  [--slice-by COL] [--threshold KEY=VALUE] [--project FILE|DIR] [--source NAME]
                  [--json] [-o REPORT.json] [--dry-run]
                  TRAIN SERVING

(experimental) Compare SERVING with TRAIN (data, or profiles): per feature the schema (missing in
serving, type changed), the null rate, the population stability index (as `shape drift --psi`;
flagged at 0.2 or more), the share of serving rows with a category never seen in training, and the
share of serving values outside the training minimum and maximum. Features are ranked by PSI. Exit
0 when nothing is flagged, 1 when a feature is flagged, 2 for unusable input. A profile holds no
values: with one, only the schema and null-rate skew are reported.

positional arguments:
  TRAIN                 training data (file or folder) or a profile
  SERVING               serving data (file or folder) or a profile

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --format {auto,csv,parquet,jsonl}
  --features COLS       comma-separated feature columns (default: all)
  --label COL           the label: left out of the features; its positive rate is compared
  --slice-by COL        repeat the measures for each value of this column (slices under
                        --threshold min_slice_rows=N rows, default 30, are pooled)
  --threshold KEY=VALUE
                        a threshold (repeatable): psi (0.2), null_rate (0.05),
                        unseen_category_share (0.01), out_of_range_share (0.01), label_rate_diff
                        (not set), min_slice_rows (30)
  --project FILE|DIR    project file shape.yml (or its folder): thresholds of
                        sources.NAME.thresholds
  --source NAME         the source of --project (default: the only one)
  --json                print the report as JSON
  -o REPORT.json, --output REPORT.json
                        write the JSON report to a file
  --dry-run             read and check the inputs and print what the command would write or send,
                        then exit 0 (2 for invalid input); nothing is written and no connection is
                        opened

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  1   a feature is flagged
  2   bad input: a missing or unreadable file, the wrong kind of file,
      or a bad argument

docs.title: shape continue
docs.text:
Stability: experimental.

usage: shape continue [-h] [--mode {3nf,star}] [--input DIR] -o DIR [--format {csv,parquet,jsonl}]
                      [--inserts INSERTS] [--update-fraction UPDATE_FRACTION]
                      [--delete-fraction DELETE_FRACTION] [--transitions FILE.json] [--seed SEED]
                      [--as-of ISO] [--json] [--daily-rows TABLE=N] [--start-date YYYY-MM-DD]
                      [--end-date YYYY-MM-DD] [--date-column TABLE.COLUMN] [--scale PRESET]
                      [--path-template TEMPLATE] [--batch-date YYYY-MM-DD]
                      [--table-format TABLE=FORMAT] [--dry-run]
                      DOMAIN|SCHEMA.json

(experimental) Read the tables of DOMAIN (one CSV, Parquet or JSON Lines file per table in
--input) and write the next delta: new rows, updated rows and soft-deleted rows, tagged with
_shape_delta_type (INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE) and _shape_delta_timestamp. New keys continue above
the existing ones; new child rows point at parents that exist after the delta. With the same data
and seed the delta is the same (--as-of fixes the timestamp).

positional arguments:
  DOMAIN|SCHEMA.json    an installed domain (see `shape list`) or a generation schema file (`shape
                        from-ddl` writes one)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --mode {3nf,star}     the schema mode of a domain
  --input DIR           the existing data, one file per table (change mode)
  -o DIR, --output DIR  where the delta files go
  --format {csv,parquet,jsonl}, -f {csv,parquet,jsonl}
                        default: csv
  --inserts INSERTS     new rows per table (default: 100)
  --update-fraction UPDATE_FRACTION
                        fraction of existing rows to update, 0-1 (default: 0.1)
  --delete-fraction DELETE_FRACTION
                        fraction of existing rows to soft-delete, 0-1 (default: 0.02)
  --transitions FILE.json
                        state transitions: {"table.column": {"state": {"next": probability}}}
  --seed SEED           the seed (default: the schema's)
  --as-of ISO           the change time on every row (default: now, UTC)
  --json                print the result as JSON
  --dry-run             read and check the inputs and print what the command would write or send,
                        then exit 0 (2 for invalid input); nothing is written and no connection is
                        opened

daily batches (instead of --input):
  Generate one day's new rows, referencing the keys of every earlier day, with no input files: a
  day is regenerable alone and the same bytes every time (docs/INCREMENTAL.md). Needs --daily-
  rows, --start-date and --batch-date.

  --daily-rows TABLE=N  new rows of TABLE per day (repeatable), e.g. customer=300 order=4000
  --start-date YYYY-MM-DD
                        the date of day 0
  --end-date YYYY-MM-DD
                        with --batch-date: write every day from --batch-date to this one (a
                        backfill)
  --date-column TABLE.COLUMN
                        a date or timestamp column set to the day (repeatable)
  --scale PRESET, -s PRESET
                        the scale of tables not in a batch

landing layout:
  --path-template TEMPLATE
                        where each table's file goes under -o, e.g.
                        '{table}/ingest_date={date}/{table}_{yyyymmdd}.{ext}' (tokens: {table}
                        {ext} {date} {yyyymmdd} {yyyy} {mm} {dd}); default:
                        {table}/ingest_date={date}/{table}_{yyyymmdd}.{ext}
  --batch-date YYYY-MM-DD
                        the business date the date tokens take (never read from the clock)
  --table-format TABLE=FORMAT
                        the format of one table (repeatable); the other tables use --format

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  2   bad input: a missing or unreadable file, the wrong kind of file,
      or a bad argument

docs.title: shape time-travel
docs.text:
Stability: experimental.

usage: shape time-travel [-h] [--mode {3nf,star}] -o DIR [--months MONTHS] [--scale PRESET]
                         [--format {csv,parquet}] [--growth-rate GROWTH_RATE]
                         [--churn-rate CHURN_RATE] [--update-fraction UPDATE_FRACTION]
                         [--seasonality MONTH=MULT,...] [--start-date YYYY-MM-DD] [--seed SEED]
                         [--json] [--dry-run]
                         DOMAIN|SCHEMA.json

(experimental) Generate DOMAIN as month 0, then evolve it for --months months with growth,
seasonality, churn and updates, writing a snapshot per month to OUTPUT/month_N/. Child rows always
point at parents that exist in the same snapshot.

positional arguments:
  DOMAIN|SCHEMA.json    an installed domain (see `shape list`) or a generation schema file (`shape
                        from-ddl` writes one)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --mode {3nf,star}     the schema mode of a domain
  -o DIR, --output DIR  where the snapshots go
  --months MONTHS       months to evolve (default: 12)
  --scale PRESET, -s PRESET
                        the scale preset of month 0
  --format {csv,parquet}, -f {csv,parquet}
  --growth-rate GROWTH_RATE
                        monthly growth (default: 0.05)
  --churn-rate CHURN_RATE
                        monthly churn (default: 0.02)
  --update-fraction UPDATE_FRACTION
                        monthly updates (default: 0.1)
  --seasonality MONTH=MULT,...
                        growth multiplier per calendar month, e.g. 11=1.5,12=2.0
  --start-date YYYY-MM-DD
  --seed SEED           the seed (default: 42)
  --json                print the result as JSON
  --dry-run             read and check the inputs and print what the command would write or send,
                        then exit 0 (2 for invalid input); nothing is written and no connection is
                        opened

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  2   bad input: a missing or unreadable file, the wrong kind of file,
      or a bad argument

docs.title: shape chaos
docs.text:
Stability: experimental.

usage: shape chaos [-h] [--mode {3nf,star}] [--input DIR] -o DIR
                   [--corrupt KIND[=RATE][@TABLE[.COLUMN]][:OPT=V,...]] [--seed SEED]
                   [--scale PRESET] [--batch BATCH] [--start-date YYYY-MM-DD]
                   [--format {csv,parquet,jsonl}] [--ground-truth FILE] [--allow-real-input]
                   [--json] [--path-template TEMPLATE] [--batch-date YYYY-MM-DD]
                   [--table-format TABLE=FORMAT] [--dry-run]
                   [DOMAIN|SCHEMA.json]

(experimental) Apply named corruptions (duplicates, orphan_keys, date_shift, negative_amounts,
case_whitespace, pii_fill, type_change, null_creep) to tables, each with a rate, and write a
machine-readable ground-truth log (JSON Lines): the table, row, key, column, before and after of
every change, with the seed. The same seed gives the same corruption and the same log.

positional arguments:
  DOMAIN|SCHEMA.json    an installed domain (see `shape list`) or a generation schema file; with
                        --input it names the keys and foreign keys, without it the tables are
                        generated

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --mode {3nf,star}     the schema mode of a domain
  --input DIR           the tables to corrupt, flat files or <table>/ingest_date=YYYY-MM-DD/<file>
  -o DIR, --output DIR  where the files go
  --corrupt KIND[=RATE][@TABLE[.COLUMN]][:OPT=V,...]
                        a corruption (repeatable), e.g. duplicates=0.02
                        orphan_keys=0.01@order.customer_id pii_fill=0.05@customer.notes
                        null_creep=0.02@order.status:step=0.01,from=3
  --seed SEED           the seed (default: the schema's, else 42)
  --scale PRESET, -s PRESET
                        the scale, when generating
  --batch BATCH         the batch number (default: from --batch-date and --start-date)
  --start-date YYYY-MM-DD
                        the date of batch 0, to derive the batch
  --format {csv,parquet,jsonl}, -f {csv,parquet,jsonl}
                        default: csv
  --ground-truth FILE   the log (default: -o/_chaos_ground_truth.jsonl)
  --allow-real-input    corrupt --input tables that are not marked as Shape-generated (listed with
                        a matching sha256 in _shape_provenance.json, or Parquet with the
                        shape_synthetic marker); the ground-truth log records input_provenance:
                        unverified
  --json                print the result as JSON
  --dry-run             read and check the inputs and print what the command would write or send,
                        then exit 0 (2 for invalid input); nothing is written and no connection is
                        opened

landing layout:
  --path-template TEMPLATE
                        where each table's file goes under -o, e.g.
                        '{table}/ingest_date={date}/{table}_{yyyymmdd}.{ext}' (tokens: {table}
                        {ext} {date} {yyyymmdd} {yyyy} {mm} {dd})
  --batch-date YYYY-MM-DD
                        the business date the date tokens take (never read from the clock)
  --table-format TABLE=FORMAT

Stability: experimental.

usage: shape rules [-h] {mutate,backtest} ...

docs.title: shape rules mutate
docs.text:
Stability: experimental.

usage: shape rules mutate [-h] [--plan PLAN.json] [--seed SEED] [--rate RATE] [--diff]
                          [--min-score S] [-o REPORT.json] [--json] [--dry-run]
                          DATA CONTRACT.json

Each mutant is one corruption of `shape chaos` on one table and column, profiled in memory and
checked against the contract (and, with --diff or a `drift` section in the contract, compared with
the unmutated profile). A mutant is killed when a rule or a drift change fires. The same seed
gives the same report.

  --dry-run             read and check the inputs and print what the command would write or send,
                        then exit 0 (2 for invalid input); nothing is written and no connection is
                        opened

docs.title: shape pack
docs.text:
Stability: stable.

usage: shape pack [-h] {run,replay,validate,list} ...

Scenario packs bundle a domain, a simulation kind (file_drop, stream or hybrid), chaos and
validation gates. A generation spec (*.gsl.yaml) points at a pack and adds schema, scale, seed,
chaos, outputs and gates.

positional arguments:
  {run,replay,validate,list}
    run                 run a pack or a spec and write its output and run manifest
    replay              regenerate a run from its manifest and check its dataset id
    validate            check a pack or a spec against its domain without running it
    list                list the packs and specs in a directory

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

docs.title: shape pack run
docs.text:
Stability: stable.

usage: shape pack run [-h] [--root DIR] [--domain DOMAIN] [--json] [--scale PRESET] [--seed SEED]
                      [--identifiers {reserved,realistic}] [-o DIR] [--dry-run]
                      PACK.yaml|SPEC.gsl.yaml

Generate the domain, apply chaos, write the files or events the pack asks for, check its
validation gates and write <run_id>_manifest.json. Exit 0 on success, 1 when the pack is invalid,
a gate fails (without chaos) or generation fails, 2 for bad input.

positional arguments:
  PACK.yaml|SPEC.gsl.yaml
                        a pack file or a generation spec; DOMAIN/PACK_ID with --root; library:NAME
                        for a starter scenario

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --root DIR            a pack directory: <DIR>/<domain>/<id>.yaml
  --domain DOMAIN       the domain to use (default: the pack's domain, or the spec's schema)
  --json                print the result as JSON
  --scale PRESET        scale preset (default: the spec's, or small)
  --seed SEED           seed (default: the spec's, or 42)
  --identifiers {reserved,realistic}
                        reserved: e-mail, URI, phone and SSN values that cannot belong to a real
                        person; realistic: values that can (never for data that leaves a test
                        system). Default: the spec's scenario.identifiers, else the schema's, else
                        reserved
  -o DIR, --output DIR  output directory (default: pack_output)
  --dry-run             read and check the inputs and print what the command would write or send,
                        then exit 0 (2 for invalid input); nothing is written and no connection is
                        opened

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  1   the pack or spec is not valid, or the run failed
  2   bad input: a missing or unreadable file, the wrong kind of file,
      or a bad argument

docs.text:

usage: shape pack replay [-h] [--root DIR] [--domain DOMAIN] [--json]

used, into a scratch directory, and compare the dataset id with the recorded one. Exit 0 when they

docs.title: shape seed
docs.text:
Stability: experimental.

usage: shape seed [-h] --target URI [--scale PRESET] [--seed SEED]
                  [--mode {create,truncate,append}] [--dry-run] [--json]
                  SPEC|DOMAIN

(experimental) Generate the tables of a domain or generation schema and write each one through the
database sink of the target's scheme (mssql or sqlserver, postgres or postgresql, mysql), parents
before the tables that point at them. A sql://DIR target writes one ordered INSERT script per
table instead. A table is one transaction (the sinks commit per table). --mode create (the
default) refuses an existing table and writes nothing; truncate empties the tables first, so the
same seed gives the same contents; append adds rows. --dry-run prints the plan and connects to
nothing. Passwords are never part of the URI: use the sink's password environment variable.

positional arguments:
  SPEC|DOMAIN           a generation schema file or a domain

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --target URI          the database URI or sql://DIR
  --scale PRESET, -s PRESET
                        a scale preset, or tiny
  --seed SEED           the seed (default: the schema's)
  --mode {create,truncate,append}
                        create refuses existing tables (default), truncate empties them, append
                        adds rows
  --dry-run             print the plan; connect to nothing
  --json                print the result as JSON

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  1   `--mode create` found an existing table, or `--mode append` a
      primary key already in its table (nothing is written)
  2   bad input: a missing or unreadable file, the wrong kind of file,
      or a bad argument

usage: shape demo run [-h] [--mode {inference,streaming,seeding}] [--connection CONNECTION]

Run a scenario. `--rows` picks the scale preset that is generated (small up to 2,000 rows, medium
