docs.title: shape fidelity
docs.text:
Stability: experimental.

usage: shape fidelity [-h] [--tolerance TOLERANCE] [--input-format {auto,csv,parquet,jsonl}]
                      [--min-score MIN_SCORE] [--min-table-score MIN_TABLE_SCORE]
                      [--min-column-score MIN_COLUMN_SCORE] [-o REPORT] [--format FORMAT]
                      [--junit FILE] [--sarif FILE] [--notify REF] [--project FILE] [--no-project]
                      [--tier {1,2,3}] [--max-auc MAX_AUC] [--min-pass-rate MIN_PASS_RATE]
                      [--expected-anomaly-rate EXPECTED_ANOMALY_RATE]
                      [--min-edge-overlap MIN_EDGE_OVERLAP] [--json] [--dry-run]
                      REFERENCE SYNTHETIC

(experimental) Compare SYNTHETIC with REFERENCE (a CSV, Parquet or JSONL file, or a directory of
one file per table; a profile is not a reference, use `shape diff`) and score every column 0-100,
then every table and the whole. Exit 0 when every pass mark is met, 1 when not, 2 for bad input.
Given a captured profile (REFERENCE.json) and a CSV file it certifies the CSV against the profile
instead (--tolerance; exit 3 on failure).

positional arguments:
  REFERENCE
  SYNTHETIC

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --tolerance TOLERANCE
                        with a REFERENCE.json profile
  --input-format {auto,csv,parquet,jsonl}
  --min-score MIN_SCORE
                        overall pass mark (default 85)
  --min-table-score MIN_TABLE_SCORE
                        per-table pass mark (default 70)
  --min-column-score MIN_COLUMN_SCORE
                        per-column pass mark (default: none)
  -o REPORT, --output REPORT
                        write a report; .json, .md or .html by extension (repeatable; a --tier
                        report is .json only)
  --format FORMAT       what to print: a shape.reports format such as json, md or html (default
                        json)
  --notify REF          also send the result to this webhook (an env:// or file:// reference to
                        its address; repeatable), on top of the notifications of shape.yml
  --json                print exactly one JSON document on standard output (format shape-result;
                        the text goes to standard error)
  --dry-run             read and check the inputs and print what the command would write or send,
                        then exit 0 (2 for invalid input); nothing is written and no connection is
                        opened

CI reports (defaults: the `ci:` block of shape.yml):
  --junit FILE          write the checks as JUnit XML
  --sarif FILE          write the findings as SARIF 2.1.0

project file (shape.yml):
  --project FILE        use this project file instead of searching
  --no-project          ignore shape.yml

tiers:
  --tier 1: mixture fits, conditional profiles, adversarial AUC, temporal profiles and
  periodicity (the adversarial and mixture parts need `pip install 'sqllocks-shape[advanced]'`);
  --tier 2: format preservation, string similarity, cardinality and anomaly-rate checks; --tier
  3: the Chow-Liu dependency tree of each side and how much of its structure the synthetic data
  keeps (experimental).

  --tier {1,2,3}        run this fidelity tier instead
  --max-auc MAX_AUC     tier 1: the adversarial AUC must stay below this (default 0.75)
  --min-pass-rate MIN_PASS_RATE
                        tier 2: share of the checks that must pass (default 1.0)
  --expected-anomaly-rate EXPECTED_ANOMALY_RATE
                        tier 2: the expected share of rows flagged in _shape_is_anomaly (default
                        0)
  --min-edge-overlap MIN_EDGE_OVERLAP
                        tier 3: least overlap of the two dependency trees' edges (default: no
                        gate)

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  1   a pass mark was missed
  2   bad input: a missing or unreadable file, the wrong kind of file,
      or a bad argument
  3   with a REFERENCE.json profile: the certificate failed

docs.title: shape check
docs.text:
Stability: stable.

usage: shape check [-h] [--data DATA] [--format {auto,csv,parquet,jsonl}] [--json RESULT.json]
                   [--junit FILE] [--sarif FILE] [--notify REF] [--project FILE] [--no-project]
                   [--source NAME] [--changes FILE] [--no-changes] [--on YYYY-MM-DD] [--strict]
                   [--enforce-learned] [--verify PUBKEY] [--dry-run]
                   PROFILE.shape [CONTRACT.json]

Check a profile (or a captured evidence document) against a contract. Exit 0 when it passes, 1
when a profile fails it, 4 when an evidence document fails it, 2 for bad input.

positional arguments:
  PROFILE.shape
  CONTRACT.json         default: the `contract` of the source in shape.yml

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --data DATA           a data file or directory of data files: needed by the contract's
                        `timeseries` and `reconcile` rules, which check data rather than the
                        profile
  --format {auto,csv,parquet,jsonl}
  --json RESULT.json
  --notify REF          also send the result to this webhook (an env:// or file:// reference to
                        its address; repeatable), on top of the notifications of shape.yml
  --strict              every broken rule fails the check, whatever its strength (exit 1)
  --enforce-learned     a broken rule of strength 'learned' fails the check like a hard one
                        (without it, it is a warning)
  --verify PUBKEY       require every .shape input to be signed by this public key: a file, -
                        (standard input), env://VAR, file://PATH or kv://... (exit 1 if not)
  --dry-run             read and check the inputs and print what the command would write or send,
                        then exit 0 (2 for invalid input); nothing is written and no connection is
                        opened

CI reports (defaults: the `ci:` block of shape.yml):
  --junit FILE          write the checks as JUnit XML
  --sarif FILE          write the findings as SARIF 2.1.0

project file (shape.yml):
  --project FILE        use this project file instead of searching
  --no-project          ignore shape.yml
  --source NAME         the source of shape.yml whose settings apply

planned changes (shape-changes.yml):
  --changes FILE        the planned-change file (default: the `changes` key of shape.yml, else
                        shape-changes.yml next to it); see docs/PLANNED_CHANGES.md
  --no-changes          ignore planned changes
  --on YYYY-MM-DD       the date planned changes are active on (default: today, UTC)

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  1   a contract rule failed on a profile, or a `--verify` public key
      does not verify an input, or an input's signature is invalid
  2   a rule needs a value a safe capture left out and nothing is
      violated (not evaluable), or bad input: a missing or unreadable
      file, the wrong kind of file, or a bad argument
  4   a contract rule failed on a Shape model or evidence document

usage: shape drift [-h] [--psi] [--threshold THRESHOLD] [--pvalue PVALUE]
                   [--input-format {auto,csv,parquet,jsonl}] [-o REPORT] [--json] [--dry-run]
                   REFERENCE CURRENT

With --psi each column is scored by its population stability index alone (no SciPy needed);

docs.title: shape registry
docs.text:
Stability: stable.

usage: shape registry [-h] ROOT ACTION ...

Keep named, content-addressed versions of artifacts in a directory. `shape registry ROOT ACTION
...`. A raw profile holds real values and is refused: commit the safe form (--safe, or the output
of `shape profile safe`). This is not `shape profile registry`, the catalog of named profiles.

positional arguments:
  ROOT        the registry directory (created when missing)
  ACTION
    commit    record a new version of NAME
    checkout  write a version of NAME to a file
    tag       give a version of NAME a tag
    promote   point the ref TARGET at the version SOURCE of NAME
    log       every commit of NAME, oldest first
    list      the names in the registry
    show      one log entry of NAME
    diff      what changed between two versions of NAME (drift with severity for two profiles)
    prune     remove log entries and objects older than a date (keeps referenced and tagged ones)

options:

docs.text:
Stability: stable.

usage: shape registry ROOT prune [-h] --before DATE [--name NAME] [--keep-last N] [--dry-run]
                                 [--json]

Remove the log entries committed before --before, then the objects that no remaining entry, ref or
tag of any name points at. Every version a ref (latest, a promoted ref) or a tag points at is
kept, and so are the newest --keep-last entries of each name. Pruning cannot be undone: try --dry-
run first. Exit 0 done (or dry run), 2 bad input (a bad date, an unknown name, a bad --keep-last,
a held prune.lock). See docs/REGISTRY.md.

options:
  -h, --help     show this help message and exit
  --before DATE  remove entries committed strictly before this instant: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC)
                 or an ISO 8601 timestamp with Z or an offset
  --name NAME    prune the log of this name only (repeatable; default: every name)
  --keep-last N  always keep the newest N entries of each name (default 1; at least 1)
  --dry-run      report what would go; change nothing
  --json         print the report as JSON (format shape-registry-prune, version 1)

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  2   bad input: a missing or unreadable file, the wrong kind of file,
      or a bad argument

docs.title: shape bisect
docs.text:
Stability: experimental.

usage: shape bisect [-h] --good REF --bad REF [--column COL] [--kind KIND] [--contract FILE]
                    [--verify-all] [--coarse {week,month}] [--json] [--project FILE]
                    [--no-project] [--source NAME] [--null-rate NULL_RATE]
                    [--cardinality-ratio-max CARDINALITY_RATIO_MAX]
                    [--cardinality-ratio-min CARDINALITY_RATIO_MIN]
                    [--mean-shift-std MEAN_SHIFT_STD] [--min-severity MIN_SEVERITY]
                    [--threshold KEY=VALUE] [--column-threshold COLUMN:KEY=VALUE]
                    [--ignore COL1,COL2] [--only COL1,COL2] [--policy POLICY.json]
                    REGISTRY NAME

(experimental) Binary search over the versions of NAME in a registry, between --good and --bad
(registry refs), for the first version that tests bad. The default test is `shape diff` against
the good version, under the thresholds and ignore lists of the shape.yml source (flags override);
--contract FILE tests 'the contract fails' instead. Exit 0 when found, 2 when --good tests bad,
--bad tests good, or a version cannot be tested. `shape bisect layers ...` finds the layer of a
pipeline where a change appears (see `shape bisect layers --help`). See docs/HISTORY.md.

positional arguments:
  REGISTRY              the registry directory
  NAME                  the committed name whose versions are searched

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --good REF            a version known to be good
  --bad REF             a later version known to be bad
  --column COL          only changes of this column count
  --kind KIND           only changes of this diff kind count
  --contract FILE       a version is bad when this contract fails
  --verify-all          test every version instead of bisecting, and report any that flips back to
                        good
  --coarse {week,month}
                        bisect over merged windows first (profiles need `shape profile
                        --sketches`)
  --json                print the result as JSON

project file (shape.yml):
  --project FILE        use this project file instead of searching
  --no-project          ignore shape.yml
  --source NAME         the source of shape.yml whose settings apply

drift thresholds (defaults: docs/DRIFT.md):
  --null-rate NULL_RATE
  --cardinality-ratio-max CARDINALITY_RATIO_MAX
  --cardinality-ratio-min CARDINALITY_RATIO_MIN
  --mean-shift-std MEAN_SHIFT_STD
  --min-severity MIN_SEVERITY
  --threshold KEY=VALUE
                        any threshold by name (repeatable), e.g. --threshold category_tvd=0.2
  --column-threshold COLUMN:KEY=VALUE
                        a threshold for the columns COLUMN matches (a name, table.column or a
                        glob)
  --ignore COL1,COL2    columns to leave out (table.column ok)
  --only COL1,COL2      compare only these columns
  --policy POLICY.json  thresholds, "columns", "ignore" and "only" in one JSON file (a contract's
                        "drift" object works)

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  2   `--good` tests bad, `--bad` tests good, or a version cannot be
      tested, or bad input: a missing or unreadable file, the wrong
      kind of file, or a bad argument

docs.title: shape contracts check-consumers
docs.text:
Stability: experimental.

usage: shape contracts check-consumers [-h] [--consumers DIR] [--baseline BASE.shape]
                                       [--require-consumers] [-o REPORT.json] [--json]
                                       [--project FILE] [--no-project] [--source NAME] [--dry-run]
                                       PROFILE.shape

Run the consumer contracts in DIR (default contracts/consumers/ next to shape.yml) whose `source`
matches against PROFILE.shape, and report each consumer as pass or fail with its violations, its
owner and the producer's column owners. With --baseline, also mark which violations are new: rules
that passed on the baseline and fail on the profile. Exit 0 when every consumer passes, 1 when one
fails, 2 for unusable input.

positional arguments:
  PROFILE.shape

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --consumers DIR       default: contracts/consumers/
  --baseline BASE.shape
                        the profile before the change
  --require-consumers   exit 2 when no consumer contract matches the source
  -o REPORT.json, --output REPORT.json
                        write the report as JSON
  --json                print the report as JSON, not text
  --dry-run             read and check the inputs and print what the command would write or send,
                        then exit 0 (2 for invalid input); nothing is written and no connection is
                        opened

project file (shape.yml):
  --project FILE        use this project file instead of searching
  --no-project          ignore shape.yml
  --source NAME         the source of shape.yml whose settings apply

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  1   a consumer contract is broken
  2   bad input: a missing or unreadable file, the wrong kind of file,
      or a bad argument

docs.title: shape parity
docs.text:
Stability: experimental.

usage: shape parity [-h] [--dataset] [--scaled] [--row-tolerance F] [--tables T,...]
                    [-o REPORT.json] [--json] [--project FILE] [--no-project] [--source NAME]
                    [--dry-run]
                    A B

(experimental) Compare two environments by shape: the same tables and columns, types, keys and
relationships, similar null rates and distributions, and table sizes in the same proportions. A
and B are data (a file or a folder), a .shape profile, a `shape profile export` file or a `shape
profile safe` file. A check the inputs cannot support is reported as not measured, never as a
pass. Exit 0 parity, 1 a check failed, 2 unusable input.

positional arguments:
  A                     the reference side (for example production)
  B                     the side under test (for example development)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --dataset             a folder is several tables, one per file (as for `shape profile`)
  --scaled              compare each table's share of the total row count, so a smaller
                        environment with the same proportions passes
  --row-tolerance F     how far row counts (or, with --scaled, shares) may differ, default 0.1
  --tables T,...        compare only these tables
  -o REPORT.json, --output REPORT.json
                        write the report as JSON
  --json                print the report as JSON, not text
  --dry-run             read and check the inputs and print what the command would write or send,
                        then exit 0 (2 for invalid input); nothing is written and no connection is
                        opened

project file (shape.yml):
  --project FILE        use this project file instead of searching
  --no-project          ignore shape.yml
  --source NAME         the source of shape.yml whose settings apply

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  1   a parity check failed
  2   bad input: a missing or unreadable file, the wrong kind of file,
      or a bad argument

docs.title: shape ci post-comment
docs.text:
Stability: experimental.

usage: shape ci post-comment [-h] --body-file FILE --repo OWNER/REPO --pr N [--json] [--dry-run]

Post the comment written by `shape ci comment`. The token is read from GITHUB_TOKEN (never from an
argument) and the server from GITHUB_API_URL (default https://api.github.com). A comment of the
same author that carries the marker is updated, otherwise one is created. A 403 or 404 (a fork
pull request, whose token cannot write) prints a notice and exits 0, so the check result still
decides the gate.

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --body-file FILE
  --repo OWNER/REPO
  --pr N             pull request number
  --json             print the outcome as a shape-result
  --dry-run          read and check the inputs and print what the command would write or send,
                     then exit 0 (2 for invalid input); nothing is written and no connection is
                     opened

Exit codes:
  0   ok
  1   GitHub answered with an error other than 403 or 404 (those print

  2   bad input: a missing or unreadable file, the wrong kind of file,

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Status: available.

docs.title: Run the local examples
docs.text:
The examples below use disposable local files from this checkout. The example test environment sets SHAPE_DOCS_REPO, installs core and plugins from source, and prepares local services. Run each page in its own empty directory, in the order shown. Complete output appears beneath each command. Elapsed times, temporary paths, job IDs and generated signing keys vary; the harness validates those runtime fields and compares the remaining output exactly.

python "$SHAPE_DOCS_REPO/scripts/docs_example_setup.py" CONTRIBUTING
Output (exit 0) 
Prepared local fixtures for CONTRIBUTING

Early access 0.9.3. Profiling, contracts and drift are available and supported. Generation from a profile is available and is being hardened. Other surfaces are experimental unless labelled available. The 1.x promises describe future policy.

You contribute code and documentation under MIT. Sign off every commit with a Signed-off-by: Your Name <your email> trailer. The sign-off certifies the Developer Certificate of Origin. Use your own identity. The DCO workflow checks every commit in a pull request.

docs.title: Prepare a change
docs.text:
Open an issue for a platform, domain or feature request. Describe the input, expected output and a small reproducible case. Do not include credentials, production rows or proprietary reference assets. Maintainers review behavior against specifications and conformance tests. See governance.

Keep the published .shape format readable, deterministic behavior, sensitivity and provenance propagation, and fail-closed input handling. Core must not gain a mandatory network dependency. Add a regression test for a bug and conformance tests for new normative behavior. Document the changed behavior.

docs.title: Local development
docs.text:
Published packages support Python 3.11 or newer. The complete development and documentation environment needs Python 3.12 or newer and Rust stable 1.85 or newer to build the native kernel. Install the pinned uv version and bootstrap the locked workspace:

python3 -m pip install --user "uv==0.8.17"
make bootstrap

Bootstrap runs uv sync --locked --group docs --group dbt --group benchmark; core remains the maturin root project and the 12 first-party plugins are editable workspace members. No shell activation is needed. For core-only work on Python 3.11, use uv sync --locked. Run tools with uv run --locked, adding --group docs for documentation tools. Never run pip install in the uv development environment. After changing Rust code, run uv run --locked maturin develop --release to rebuild shape._kernel.

Edit development dependencies in [dependency-groups] in pyproject.toml, run make lock (uv lock), and commit uv.lock in the same commit. make lock-check rejects a stale lock. To deliberately upgrade one dependency, run uv lock --upgrade-package X, review the lock changes and run make bootstrap and the checks again. Published extras are retained for compatibility; do not change their ranges when editing development groups.

The Fabric SDK requires PyArrow below 20 while docs and benchmarks pin 25.0.1. These groups are explicitly incompatible in the universal lock. Run Fabric tests in a separate environment: UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv-fabric uv sync --locked --group fabric-demo, then use the same variable with uv run --locked --no-sync. Do not combine fabric-demo with docs or benchmark. Bootstrap selects the groups needed by make check.

Without uv, the unsupported-but-working fallback is a separate virtual environment:

python -m venv .venv-pip
. .venv-pip/bin/activate
make bootstrap-pip

On Windows, run make bootstrap-pip with the venv’s Python supplied through PYTHON. The fallback uses the previous pip editable install and does not provide lockfile guarantees. Run tools directly in that venv, for example python -m pytest; the other Make targets require uv.

Before submitting a change, run the repository checks:

make check

The target runs Ruff lint and format checks on src/, tests/, plugins/ and the benchmark harness, strict mypy, Vulture, import checks and the repository checks in scripts/. It also runs the core tests with their coverage floor, heavy tests, the pure-Python kernel tests, and Rust formatting, clippy and tests. The repository checks cover requirements, secrets, user-facing wording, shipped data, plugin skeletons, versions and conformance coverage. For a quicker local run:

uv run --locked pytest -m "not emulator and not live"
SHAPE_KERNEL=python uv run --locked pytest -m "not emulator and not live"

Tests marked emulator need their local services; tests marked live need configured accounts. Their CI and Nightly jobs prepare those prerequisites. Performance-sensitive changes need before and after measurements from benchmarks/, recorded only after the equivalence verifier passes on the timed output.

New normative behavior needs traceability in docs/specs/requirements.yaml and a conformance test for each affected statement in docs/specs/SHAPE_2.md. Artifact, evidence, generation, classification and query-parsing changes also need the relevant conformance or security tests. Update the affected docs in the same change.

The docs workflow installs the core and local domains and databases plugins from this checkout, runs the tutorial harness and API coverage checks, and builds MkDocs in strict mode. It also checks wording and links. Use the documentation style guide for a new page. The harness runs only blocks explicitly marked runnable, with their shown output.

A new Fabric API, item type or runtime needs its entry in the platform inventory with the shipped behavior, Microsoft Learn source and date. tests/docs/test_fabric_platform.py rejects unlisted surfaces and entries marked preview or retired. Keep account-dependent execution claims out of docs.

docs.title: Public interfaces
docs.text:
The package's shape.__all__ is the top-level public Python surface. Generated API documentation and CI cover every name and its docstring. Modules with a separate __all__ are also included. The stable modules shape.generation.spec_edit and shape.generation.spec_schema have a compatibility baseline in tests/api/stable_api_baseline.json, described in the API policy. The check python scripts/stable_api_compat.py --check runs through tests/api/test_stable_api_compat.py and make check.

  • After an additive change, run python scripts/stable_api_compat.py --write and commit the baseline. Additive changes include exported names, methods, trailing optional keyword parameters and trailing dataclass fields with defaults. The writer refuses breaking changes.
  • A breaking change needs a new major version. Keep the old member working with a DeprecationWarning until the next major version; do not erase a compatibility failure by editing the baseline.
  • Add a new exported name to the table in docs/API_STABILITY.md and the module's __all__.

See scope and limits before proposing a new feature, the CLI policy for command stability and the 1.0 checklist for the release requirements.

docs.title: Documentation site
docs.text:
Run make bootstrap with Python 3.12 or newer. requirements-docs.txt is a generated compatibility export of the docs group for the example harness and pip consumers; make docs-export-check checks it against the lock. Regenerate it with uv run --locked python scripts/check_docs_requirements.py --write after changing the lock. The site reads mkdocs.yml; its hooks generate the CLI reference from the parser, the API reference from exported names and the performance reference from committed, verified benchmark results. Do not edit generated output by hand.

List public pages in the navigation. Internal material under docs/plans/ and docs/talks/ stays outside the public site. Links to source files and examples outside docs/ are rewritten to their repository locations when the site is built. Before submitting docs changes, run:

uv run --locked --group docs mkdocs build --strict
uv run --locked --group docs python scripts/check_doc_links.py --site site
uv run --locked --group docs python scripts/check_user_facing.py --site site

Warnings fail the strict build. The link check validates source and site links; the wording check validates the public source and rendered pages.

docs.title: Review
docs.text: A pull request explains the concrete problem, changed behavior, tests and limitations. Keep code, tests and affected docs in the same change. Maintainers decide whether the change is ready; the repository owner merges. Security changes may tighten input handling. Report security issues through the security policy.

docs.title: Governance
docs.text:
Status: available.

Early access 0.9.3. Profiling, contracts and drift are available and supported. Generation from a profile is available and is being hardened. Other surfaces are experimental unless labelled available. The 1.x promises describe future policy.

SQLLocks maintains Shape. The repository owner reviews and merges contributions. Jonathan Stewart is the sole maintainer, with final review and merge authority. No review or merge authority is delegated. Owner decision, 2026-10-11.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: You propose a change in an issue or pull request with the problem, expected behavior and supporting code or tests. Maintainers review public behavior against versioned specifications and conformance tests. Accepted decisions are recorded in the issue or pull request. A breaking specification change needs a version and migration path. Security fixes may tighten behavior.

docs.title: Platform requests
docs.text: Use the platform request template. Describe whether you need reads, writes or exports, the URI and authentication model, and a local fixture or account-free test strategy. Maintainers check dependencies, credential handling, licensing and tests before accepting a new adapter. A request is not a delivery commitment. Shipped platform behavior must have documentation that matches the code; cloud targets need owner validation before commands are published.

docs.title: Domain requests
docs.text: Use the domain request template. Explain tables, keys, relationships, scales and reference-data sources. Reference data must permit redistribution and include licence and attribution evidence. Maintainers review schema tests, deterministic generation and the documented sources. An unproved calibration claim stays an owner placeholder.

docs.title: Participation
docs.text:
Follow the code of conduct. Sign off contributions under the contributing policy. Public support uses support@shapedata.ai; security reports follow SECURITY.md.

Report a problem with this page

docs.title: Security policy
docs.text:
Status: available.

Report a suspected vulnerability privately to support@shapedata.ai or use GitHub private vulnerability reporting for this repository. Include the affected version, reproducible steps and impact. Do not attach production data, credentials or private profiles to public issues. Only the latest release is supported. Responses are best-effort: no response-time commitment and no backports. Owner decision, 2026-10-11.

A safe capture is data minimisation, not anonymisation. Review profiles before sharing them. Plugins run as trusted Python code in the Shape process. See What leaves my machine for the code-backed review checklist.

docs.title: Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct
docs.text: Status: available.

docs.title: Our Pledge
docs.text:
We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, caste, color, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.

docs.title: Our Standards
docs.text:
Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment for our community include:

  • Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people
  • Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
  • Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
  • Accepting responsibility and apologizing to those affected by our mistakes, and learning from the experience
  • Focusing on what is best not just for us as individuals, but for the overall community

Examples of unacceptable behavior include:

  • The use of sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind
  • Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
  • Public or private harassment
  • Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or email address, without their explicit permission
  • Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting

docs.title: Enforcement Responsibilities
docs.text:
Community leaders are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.

Community leaders have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation decisions when appropriate.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This Code of Conduct applies within all community spaces, and also applies when an individual is officially representing the community in public spaces. Examples of representing our community include using an official e-mail address, posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text:
Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported to the community leaders responsible for enforcement at support@shapedata.ai. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly.

All community leaders are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter of any incident.

docs.title: Enforcement Guidelines
docs.text: Community leaders will follow these Community Impact Guidelines in determining the consequences for any action they deem in violation of this Code of Conduct:

docs.title: 1. Correction
docs.text:
Community Impact: Use of inappropriate language or other behavior deemed unprofessional or unwelcome in the community.

Consequence: A private, written warning from community leaders, providing clarity around the nature of the violation and an explanation of why the behavior was inappropriate. A public apology may be requested.

docs.title: 2. Warning
docs.text:
Community Impact: A violation through a single incident or series of actions.

Consequence: A warning with consequences for continued behavior. No interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, for a specified period of time. This includes avoiding interactions in community spaces as well as external channels like social media. Violating these terms may lead to a temporary or permanent ban.

docs.title: 3. Temporary Ban
docs.text:
Community Impact: A serious violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior.

Consequence: A temporary ban from any sort of interaction or public communication with the community for a specified period of time. No public or private interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, is allowed during this period. Violating these terms may lead to a permanent ban.

docs.title: 4. Permanent Ban
docs.text:
Community Impact: Demonstrating a pattern of violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior, harassment of an individual, or aggression toward or disparagement of classes of individuals.

Consequence: A permanent ban from any sort of public interaction within the community.

docs.title: Attribution
docs.text:
This Code of Conduct is adapted from the Contributor Covenant, version 2.1, available at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html.

Community Impact Guidelines were inspired by Mozilla's code of conduct enforcement ladder.

For answers to common questions about this code of conduct, see the FAQ at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/faq. Translations are available at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/translations.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
Status: available.

Early access 0.9.3. Profiling, contracts and drift are available and supported. Generation from a profile is available and is being hardened. Other surfaces are experimental unless labelled available. The 1.x promises describe future policy.

docs.title: Unreleased
docs.text:
• Refresh the locked certificate bundle for GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2 and use the prepared Playwright browser for documentation verification.

Development: the dev and CI environment is now locked with uv; user installs are unchanged.

Docs: README and Quickstart link to the Shape Playground (a recorded 0.9.3 session in the browser).

Integrations: the anonymeter extra of sqllocks-shape-integrations is withdrawn; Anonymeter 1.x requires NumPy < 1.27 and Shape requires NumPy >= 2, so the extra could not be installed. The adapter stays and explains this when Anonymeter is missing.

Fix: shape diff now refuses safe profiles instead of reporting no changes (they cannot be diffed, as docs/PROJECT.md states).

Fix: shape validate accepts v1 contracts; unknown contract rules are now errors instead of being ignored; CONTRACTS.md lists every rule (including valid_as).

Fix (privacy): safe profiles no longer keep an excluded column's name or a sensitive column's fitted distribution, whatever path built them.

Converting a full capture to the safe form now gives a different content ID when the profile has sensitive columns, because their fitted distributions are no longer kept.

  • Correct Fabric plugin PyPI installation guidance and align GitHub Action status with the experimental CI capability.
  • Keep the GitHub Action comment source label when a missing baseline leaves no project annotation in the result.
  • Clarify that Excel sentinel findings include typed date/datetime cells and cover six 9999-12-31 datetime cells with a regression test.
  • Read standard dated landing layouts in shape chaos --input, preserving table names and provenance checks.
  • Changed: shape plan now prints human-readable text by default; scripts that parse its output must add --json (the JSON keys are unchanged).
0.9.2 was published to TestPyPI only and was never released to PyPI; its changes are part of 0.9.3.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Synapse dedicated SQL pool live test. The Fabric plugin ships a live test that writes to a real Synapse dedicated SQL pool, driven by SHAPE_TEST_SYNAPSE_URI, SHAPE_TEST_SYNAPSE_STAGING and the service-principal settings SHAPE_TEST_SYNAPSE_TENANT_ID, SHAPE_TEST_SYNAPSE_CLIENT_ID and SHAPE_TEST_SYNAPSE_CLIENT_SECRET. The fabric-live workflow resumes the pool before the tests and pauses it afterwards.
  • --source-config KEY=REF (global option). Passes an Azure read credential to a command by reference. KEY is token, account_key, sas_token or connection_string; REF is an env://, file:// or kv:// reference. A literal secret is refused, and the value lives only for that command.
  • --lakehouse-schema NAME on shape generate --scale-mode fabric_spark and shape demo init. Writes the tables into a schema of a schema-enabled Lakehouse.
  • --table-prefix now works with the Delta sink and with the database and Fabric destinations (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, Databricks, SQL Server, Warehouse, Synapse, SQL database, Lakehouse, Eventhouse). Where a destination cannot honour a prefix, the command stops before writing and says so, instead of ignoring the option.
  • Two timeout settings for Fabric SQL writes. SHAPE_SQL_QUERY_TIMEOUT (whole seconds, default 900) limits each SQL statement of the Warehouse, SQL database and Synapse writers, so a stalled load fails instead of waiting forever. SHAPE_WAREHOUSE_INSERT_SECONDS (whole seconds, default 600) limits how long the slower row-by-row Warehouse fallback may take per table. A value that is not a whole number is ignored and the default applies.

docs.title: Verified
docs.text: • Kerberos sign-in. Shape 0.9.1 --auth kerberos was verified on 2026-10-12 against a lab Active Directory domain with SQL Server 2022 (Windows authentication only), from an Ubuntu 24.04 client: 21,750 rows in 9 tables, exit 0, and the server recorded auth_scheme = KERBEROS. A keytab with mode 644 and a wrong principal both exit 2. No code changed for this.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Nested columns (issue #1). shape profile now profiles Parquet, Delta and JSON Lines tables that hold list, struct or map columns, where it stopped with unhashable type: nested Arrow column. The profile records the column's exact Arrow type, its null rate and, for a list or a map, the distribution of its lengths; the other columns are unchanged. diff, check, inspect and generate --from work on such a profile, and generate writes the column with the same Arrow type. generate stops with an error that names the column for a union, extension, run-end encoded or view type inside a nested column, and shape fidelity refuses a nested column by name. An error whose message holds a backtrace is now one shape: error: line.
  • Local Delta tables no longer hang at exit. shape profile (and every read of a local Delta table) could hang, or abort with terminate called without an active exception, as the process ended after a failed read (for example a damaged data file or a nested column). A local table is now read through Arrow's own file system.
  • shape profile-model / semantic-model://. A table the semantic model cannot read stops with one error naming the model and table and suggesting a refresh, instead of the raw sempy/ADOMD error.
  • Warehouse and Synapse primary keys. Fabric Warehouse rejected a primary key written inside CREATE TABLE (error 24584). Shape now creates the table first and then adds the key with ALTER TABLE ... PRIMARY KEY NONCLUSTERED ... NOT ENFORCED. SQL Server and Azure SQL keep their enforced keys.
  • Time ranges stay text. A column of values such as 18:00-18:59 is no longer read as a UTC offset when profiling; it stays text.
  • Profiling a database with zoned text dates. shape profile-db no longer stops at a sampled text column that holds dates with a time zone. The column keeps its SQL type and statistics, is left out of relationship inference, and carries a profiling_note saying so.
  • Schema-enabled Lakehouses. Tables are written under Tables/<schema>/<table>, where the SQL endpoint and semantic models can see them. Shape asks Fabric which kind of Lakehouse the target is, uses dbo unless you give a schema, refuses a schema for a classic Lakehouse, and, when it cannot tell, stops and tells you to set schema_enabled=true|false. Before, the Delta sink assumed a classic Lakehouse and wrote the tables where schema-enabled Lakehouses could not see them. Writing uses one extra read call to Fabric. This needs a credential; with only a raw storage token, give the schema in the path (.../Tables/dbo).
  • Missing Delta tables are reported as no Delta table at <path>, with credentials removed from the path.
  • The abfss:// sink writes into a Fabric Lakehouse. It used to fail with OperationNotAllowedOnThePath, because it checked for the Lakehouse with a request OneLake refuses on an item folder. It now finds the Lakehouse in the workspace listing. A Lakehouse given by GUID is no longer checked up front; a missing one is reported by the first write.
  • MySQL without TLS. The caching_sha2_password sign-in crash is replaced by a message that says to use verified TLS (ssl_ca=PATH&ssl-mode=VERIFY_CA) or ask the administrator for a supported authentication method. Shape does not fetch an untrusted key.
  • Azure storage credentials. Storage environment keys are now used in a fixed order: explicit options, then AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_KEY, AZURE_STORAGE_SAS_TOKEN, AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING, then the Fabric or Synapse notebook identity, then DefaultAzureCredential. An ambient account key no longer overrides the identity you selected for OneLake. A sign-in error that cannot succeed on retry (a tenant mismatch or a disabled account, for example) now fails once with one clear message; timeouts and throttling still retry.
  • Warehouse loads when COPY INTO fails. When OneLake cannot supply the storage token (SQL error 13840), the load falls back to parameterized INSERT in batches of 5,000 rows, keeping keys, write modes, rollback and the loaded-row check. The fallback is slower and is no longer silent: it prints a WARNING on stderr, records the note in WriteResult.notes and summary(), and fails with a rollback past SHAPE_WAREHOUSE_INSERT_SECONDS. Batched inserts now size text columns from the whole batch, not the first row, so they no longer fall back to one round trip per row. Emptied OneLake staging folders are removed after a load.
  • Fabric notebook deploy. Fabric sometimes answers with a long-running operation address on a regional *.analysis.windows.net host. Shape now polls the Fabric API for that operation instead of refusing it, and never sends your token to the other host.
  • Fabric errors say what happened. Errors show the HTTP status and Fabric's code and message, with secrets removed. A failed Spark job keeps Fabric's error code and details, or says Fabric gave no reason.
  • Fabric portal connection strings. The ADO.NET-style string from the Fabric portal (Data Source=...;Initial Catalog=...) is accepted by the SQL writers and shape profile-db.
  • Semantic models for service principals. If Fabric's direct lookup fails for a service principal, Shape lists models over REST and warns that it did.
  • Synapse. The dedicated-pool writer sends its DDL in autocommit, stages timestamps in Parquet as INT96, and writes NaN and infinite values as NULL.
  • Fabric Git sync test. The nightly job and fabric-live use FABRIC_GIT_WORKSPACE_ID (the Git-connected workspace) in place of FABRIC_WORKSPACE_ID; tenant, client and remote are variables, the client secret and Git token stay secrets. This affects people who run the live tests, not users of the package.
  • shape profile validate --safe and wide or multi-table profiles. Multi-table --dataset profiles and single wide tables now validate clean. A profile records which columns an internal sample covered as positions, sampling.internal[].column_indexes, in place of names (columns). The profile format version is unchanged, and profiles written by 0.9.1 still load and report the same findings until you profile again. Profile content ids change for the same data.
  • Privacy. A scenario pack's stream topic emits only its payload_fields columns, and pack validate rejects a field that is not a column. A pack run creates its manifest exclusively, so two runs in the same second keep their own manifests. shape chaos --input and shape incremental --input skip the ground-truth logs of an earlier chaos run and name a file that cannot be read as a table. shape registry ROOT commit runs its leak scan on any JSON document with tables, so removing redaction_manifest no longer lets a leaking profile through. shape.yml gates.NAME.mode also accepts the four gates only shape verify runs (reconciliation, timeseries_quality, memorization, utility). shape fabric setup names shape fabric notebook in its next steps.
  • VS Code "Compare with Git HEAD". The comparison document now opens; the custom editor had claimed it and no diff appeared.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Default Lakehouse name for shape fabric setup is shape_lakehouse (was shape-lakehouse). Fabric rejects the hyphen with HTTP 400. Names must begin with a letter and use only letters, digits and underscores (at most 123 characters); Shape now checks this before any request.
  • Replaced the 49 bundled AMA CPT procedure values and descriptions with synthetic SP-01 through SP-49 and Synthetic procedure NN. The letters and hyphen distinguish these five-character codes from CPT formats. Arrow schema, row count, charges and selection weights are unchanged. Healthcare examples and exact writer fixtures now use synthetic procedures and a two-character synthetic sample modifier (S0), with local FHIR code systems. The extra sample procedure outside the catalog is SP-50.
  • Replaced bundled GICS sector codes/names and industry names with a generic synthetic taxonomy (SA through SK, Synthetic sector A through Synthetic sector K, and synthetic industry labels), including company classifications. Schemas, identifiers and cardinalities are preserved. Legacy reference aliases remain readable.
  • Seeded output changes: healthcare and capital-markets generation produces new procedure/classification labels and dataset ids with the same seed. Regenerate fixtures for those domains. GENERATION_STABILITY.md, API_STABILITY.md and RELEASE_POLICY.md reserve cross-release compatibility promises for future 1.x releases and exclude domain reference data from the generator content promise; this early-access patch changes no generator algorithm or format version. Exact affected writer fixtures were regenerated.
  • Owner decisions: the synthetic replacements follow the Owner's decisions recorded in docs/plans/OWNER_DECISIONS.md (GICS taxonomy and the 49 CPT codes replaced by synthetic values in 0.9.2), and resolve the healthcare and capital-markets upstream-source owner notes in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. Other domain owner notes remain unresolved.
  • Core and all twelve first-party plugins advance together to 0.9.2. Exact SQL headers and documented artifact/registry digests were regenerated for the new writer version.

docs.title: Internal and CI (no change to the package or CLI)
docs.text:
• The regression comparison that the benchmark and nightly parity jobs run now uses the recorded output of the published Shape 0.9.1 release as its baseline; the old comparison engine is no longer installed. docs/PERFORMANCE.md joins the documentation site. Nothing you install or run changes.
  • The macOS bounded-memory tests measure the live heap peak instead of resident size, with the same inputs, floor and 10% tolerance. Test change only.
  • The documentation site gains the "Published receipts" pages (Owner-run evidence for the documented examples) and the decisions page.
  • The Fabric test fakes now enforce Warehouse DDL rules and both Lakehouse table layouts, and the live tests run unattended in the fabric-live workflow. Test and workflow change only.
Release date: 2026-10-11

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• CI provisions the executable documentation's pinned environment and released plugins, and restores the Fabric talk kit and its unmeasured live-timings placeholder.
  • Safe-profile validation handles JSON row counts larger than a floating-point number without crashing, while retaining the minimum cohort check.
  • Bounded CSV profiling avoids CPU-scaled decoded read-ahead buffers.
  • Bounded profiling reclaims freed allocator pages after each batch, including on macOS; its RSS regression test fixes Arrow's serial-reader executor sizes to avoid allocator scheduling noise.
  • Fabric setup reports portable source paths, and Synapse derives table labels from Windows paths.
  • Eventhouse emitters and writers synchronize streaming schema caches before ingesting into newly created or changed tables.
  • Eventhouse truncate and replace wait for streamed rows to be sealed, using a configurable command timeout instead of the shorter ingestion timeout.

  • Eventhouse replacement resets rows and column types while preserving table identity, avoiding stale streaming routes after dropping and recreating a table.

  • shape share-bundle verify bounds every member of a bundle before reading it (#684): at most 10,000 members, 8 MiB for attestation.json and manifest.json, 2 GiB per data file and 8 GiB in total, and no member or total that inflates more than 100 times once past 16 MiB (the Excel reader's zip-bomb guard). The limits are checked against the declared sizes and again while inflating, so a header that understates a size is caught too. A bundle over a limit exits 2 naming the member and the limit and leaves nothing extracted; before, a 40 KB bundle could inflate to more than a gigabyte. See docs/SHARE_BUNDLE.md.

  • shape-databases: a credential option (Microsoft Entra sign-in to Azure Database for PostgreSQL or MySQL) now asks for a token for https://ossrdbms-aad.database.windows.net/.default, the scope Microsoft documents for both servers. The default was https://ossrh-postgresql.azure.com/.default, which Entra does not know, so credential= failed unless token_scope was also given (#339). token_scope still overrides the default, for example for the US Gov or China clouds.
  • The leak scan (shape registry ROOT commit, shape profile validate --safe) no longer reads a whole value that is a valid ISO 8601 date or timestamp, such as a datetime column's minimum or maximum (2026-07-08 00:01:07), as a phone number. Daily profiles of a timestamp column were refused when the hour made the digits look like a phone number (F-12). A phone number anywhere else, including after a timestamp in the same value, is still refused.
  • Release engineering (P8-04, docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md): scripts/check_versions.py checks that every place a release version is written agrees (core and plugin versions, every first-party == pin, __version__, the kernel's Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock; --tag, --expect, --release), and scripts/set_version.py changes them all at once. scripts/build_release_dist.py builds the pure wheel, the core sdist and every plugin's wheel and sdist, and checks a full release set (every T-04 platform wheel). scripts/release_sbom.py writes a CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM per archive (with the kernel's Rust crates for the archives that carry it), SHA256SUMS, and the resolved SBOM of sqllocks-shape[all]. scripts/release_index_check.py checks that an index serves exactly the built files, and scripts/release_smoke.py installs sqllocks-shape[all] from TestPyPI, PyPI or a directory and runs the smoke suite. scripts/check_release_workflows.py enforces the release workflows' trusted publishing, SBOM and attestation rules. The packaging lockstep test now also checks the sqllocks-shape-healthcare-* pins, which its pattern had missed.

  • Generated values are the same bits on every CPU and platform (W8-04b, #768), so W1-15's pinned fixtures (#92) and W8-04's byte-identical files (#567) hold on Linux, macOS and Windows alike. numpy's float64 log, exp, log1p, power and cos round differently on AVX-512 CPUs and between the C libraries of each platform; every logarithm, exponential, power and cosine that makes a generated value is now computed with shape.kernel.pmath (fdlibm's algorithms with IEEE basic operations only; native kernel functions pm_log, pm_exp, pm_pow and pm_cos_turns, with numpy twins that give the same bits; docs/GENERATION_KERNEL.md, "Portable math"). This covers the normal draw itself (philox_normal, which now agrees between the kernels bit for bit), every continuous distribution family, the tables of the discrete ones, empirical's interpolation, fan-out weights, skewed foreign keys and lead times. The distributions are unchanged; the last bits of some values changed once: the pinned ids of distribution, normal and the beta, exponential, gamma, log_normal, normal, pareto, power_law_cutoff and weibull families, 77 files of the golden byte corpus, and the hr and healthcare domain outputs, and the vault test's profile-fitted CSV digest (the implementation tests lists old and new ids). Those ids already differed between CI's machines before; now they are the same on Linux, macOS (arm64) and Windows. formula expressions keep numpy's np_log, np_exp and float powers (they equal numpy's own evaluation), and specs fitted to a profile are not covered (docs/GENERATION_STABILITY.md).

  • shape pack run (PackRunner.run) refuses a domain name that is a path (a separator, .., a drive, : or another name is_safe_name refuses) with unsafe domain name '<name>': it must be a plain name, not a path, before anything is generated or written, not even the output directory; it no longer turns such a name into a safe run id (lead decision E2, #281). A scale name keeps the earlier behaviour: its part of the run id is made plain. The registry's raw-profile check (is_raw_profile, profile_capture) refuses a .shape container whose manifest no Shape reader accepts, for example one above the manifest size limit, with RegistryError: not a Shape container: ..., without inflating it (lead decision E1, #283, #396).

  • Registry pruning (#566, docs/REGISTRY.md "Pruning"): shape registry ROOT prune --before DATE [--name NAME ...] [--keep-last N] [--dry-run] [--json] and LocalRegistry.prune(before, *, names=None, keep_last=1, dry_run=False) remove log entries committed strictly before the cutoff and then the objects no remaining entry, ref or tag of any name points at. Every entry a ref (latest, promoted refs) or tag points at, and the newest keep_last entries of each name, are kept; files under objects/ that are not content ids are left alone and reported. The report (format shape-registry-prune, version 1) gives the entries removed and kept per name and why, the objects removed and the bytes freed (under --json, the payload of the shape-result document); --dry-run changes nothing. Logs are replaced atomically and objects deleted only after every log, so an interrupted prune leaves a working registry and a second prune finishes it. A prune holds prune.lock; commits, tag and promote refuse to run while it is held, and a prune waits for commits already writing. Exit 0 done, 2 bad input. Pruning cannot be undone.

  • Test suite (AUD-tests): tests no longer depend on the order they run in (shared Spark session and JVM, shared generation case schemas, a cached test module, the process-wide sys.modules and PYSPARK_PYTHON; #77, #328, #329, #330, #335); the Python-kernel Spark executor test now runs the Python kernel (#328); the suite passes on pyarrow 19.0.1 (#333); a benchmark-harness test no longer writes $BENCH_OUT_DIR (#332); only the delta-fallback tests that read through DuckDB need its downloaded extension (#331). New tests cover shape.quality.evaluate, shape.privacy.assess_summary, contract save/load, the GeoNames and Gazetteer loaders and DatetimeProfile merge.

  • Test coverage counts code the tests run in a child Python process (#337): [tool.coverage.run] patch = ["subprocess"], and the dev extra requires coverage>=7.10. shape.quality.evaluate fails a range rule whose observed value cannot be compared with the bound, instead of raising TypeError.

  • Changed (#721): the Fabric User Data Functions withhold the raw values of classified columns by default, as the bridge's profile, check and diff do. In the results of profileLakehouseFile, profileLakehouseTable and profileDataFrame a column the safe-profile gate classifies (pii_gate_fires: a personal-data pattern such as email or SSN, or nearly every value distinct) has "min": null, "max": null, "redacted": true; the violations of checkProfile and the changes of diffProfiles about such a column have observed (or baseline and current) withheld the same way, in the result and in the raised error. A new optional parameter includeRawValues (default false; include_raw_values in shape.integrations.fabric.udf) returns the raw values. Unclassified columns, existing calls and the .shape file written to outputPath are unchanged.

  • One switch for realistic identifiers (W8-06, #766, docs/GENERATION_STRATEGIES.md). Reserved identifiers stay the default; shape.generate(..., identifiers="realistic"), --identifiers realistic on shape generate (with --from and --scale-mode too), shape composite, shape demo run and shape pack run, a scenario spec's scenario.identifiers, the bridge generate command's optional identifiers argument (1.2) and a schema's top-level "identifiers" turn realistic e-mail addresses, URIs, phone numbers and SSNs on for a whole run. A column's own domains or range wins, then the run switch, then the schema, then reserved; any other value is refused. A realistic run says so once on standard error, and pack run records the mode in the run manifest (reproducibility.identifiers; a manifest without it reads and replays as reserved). The same seed and mode give the same values in both kernels and in the multiprocess and Spark workers; the default output is unchanged. The faker package's e-mail, URL, host and phone providers (the faker strategy) are reserved by default too: faker is at generator version 2, and a spec pinned at faker 1 keeps the package's values (docs/GENERATION_STABILITY.md).

  • shape seed --mode append refuses, before anything is written, a generated primary key that is already in its table (exit 1, the table and the key named; use --mode truncate to replace the rows). It used to write the tables before the clashing one and fail on the database's key (Duplicate entry '1' for key 'customer.PRIMARY' on MySQL). The shape-databases sinks gain keys_sql.

  • A floating column declared integer (the DDL makes it BIGINT) reaches the PostgreSQL and MySQL sinks as int64, and a value that is not whole is refused with the column named (PostgreSQL's COPY refused 3.0 for order_line.quantity in shape seed).

  • The sql writer's format_version is 2 (it was 1): a PostgreSQL literal with a backslash is now an E'...' literal (#285), which changes the bytes of such a script for the same input (docs/GENERATION_STABILITY.md); the golden byte corpus is rewritten.

  • Security fixes (SEC-high, the high-severity findings open at Gate G7): SQL scripts cannot gain a statement from data: in the contract and design DDL a table, schema or column name with a control character is refused and a T-SQL text value with a line break is written as N'a' + NCHAR(10) + N'b'; the SQL sink keeps the T-SQL rule above (a name with a line break is refused, a value is split only at a GO line); a PostgreSQL literal with a backslash is an E'...' literal that reads the same whatever standard_conforming_strings says (#724, #285); the single-table Excel sink stores =... and #N/A text as text, drops characters XML cannot hold and makes the sheet name valid (#629); the Fabric API, OneLake and Eventhouse transports follow a redirect only on the request's own origin, so the bearer token never reaches another host (#275); an abfss:// URI gets a storage credential only on an Azure Storage or OneLake host (#276); the bridge withholds the values, message and detail of a diff change or check violation about a classified column, joint-analysis entries included, and leaves the actual extreme of a classified column out of verify messages (#533, #535; a column that is not classified keeps the frozen, documented 1.1 message text); the demo comparison page shows no value of a classified column (#663); the shape-fabric tape scrubber redacts quoted, braced and JSON secrets, and a tape that holds a secret is refused on load as well as on save (#411); release_for suppresses small cells inside the joint block when nothing is above the target (#650); and a safe-profile column with fewer non-null rows than its k releases no value statistic, which shape profile validate --safe reports as small-cohort-statistic (#395); the safe-profile parity harness names that difference and checks it on both sides (the column is below k by the raw counts, the product holds null, the baseline's mean and std are the raw profile's).

  • shape diff on the terminal is bounded; --json FILE writes the file only (#308). On a terminal, a change's baseline/current list or mapping of more than 20 entries (a new_categorical_values change of a column with thousands of values) prints its first 20, with the count left out under values_omitted and a line on stderr; a pipe still gets the complete result. The demo's day-1/day-2 orders diff shows about 2 KB on a terminal instead of 1.1 MB. --json FILE writes the complete result to the file and prints nothing on standard output (it used to print the same document as well); --json - and the ci.json of shape.yml still carry the complete document. Capture diffs with --json OUT also write only the file. A diff's notes are also printed on stderr (shape: note: ...). See docs/CLI.md and docs/DRIFT.md.

  • [faker] extra (#309). Learned schemas use fake-data providers, so generating from one can need faker. It is the core's new [faker] extra (also in [all] and in the pure wheel's extras), the domains plugin depends on it (the healthcare demo inference now works in a clean install from the wheels), and the error without it names pip install 'sqllocks-shape[faker]'.

  • The Fabric plugin's Event Hubs and SQL Server parts are extras (#310). sqllocks-shape-fabric now needs only the core; [sqlserver] brings sqllocks-shape-sqlserver (and pyodbc) for the SQL database, Warehouse, Synapse and SQL Server targets, and [eventhubs] brings sqllocks-shape-eventhubs for the Eventstream emitter and writer. Without them every entry point still loads, and the part that needs one fails with the line to install it. pip install sqllocks-shape-fabric alone no longer brings either plugin: ask for 'sqllocks-shape-fabric[sqlserver,eventhubs]' to keep the old set (the shape demo notebook install cell does). docs/INSTALL.md and docs/DEMO.md give the install from the release's wheels (--find-links), since the plugins are not on PyPI.

  • Container image (PF-05): the image is now under the 500 MB limit measured uncompressed (about 471 MB, from 523 MB; 168 MB compressed). The build stage installs the wheel with [azure] into a prefix, strips its shared objects (strip --strip-unneeded, not the auditwheel *.libs folders) and restores the library symlinks pip unpacks as copies; the runtime stage copies only that prefix and fails the build if any shared object no longer loads. scripts/image_size.py measures an image's uncompressed size from docker save, independent of the image store (docker image inspect .Size is the compressed size under the containerd store).

  • Fabric platform inventory (docs/FABRIC_PLATFORM.md, W7-01): one table of every Fabric and OneLake REST path, item type, Spark runtime and storage endpoint that Shape calls, with its release stage, Microsoft Learn source and check date. tests/docs/test_fabric_platform.py (guard in scripts/fabric_platform.py, also runnable by hand) fails when the code builds an unlisted Fabric path or item type, or one listed preview or retired, and when a doc or plugin README names an unlisted Fabric runtime or one past its end of support. New live check plugins/shape-fabric/tests/test_live_git_sync.py (Fabric Git sync with a shape/ folder of .shape files; needs the O-02 secrets, not yet run) and the shape-live-check result format (shape_fabric.livecheck, format version 1), which declares format, version, shape_version and min_shape_version and is read through shape.compat.check_readable (state and compatibility policy).

  • Security fixes: the Fabric clients (shape.scale Spark router, the shape-fabric plugin's Items API) follow a Location or continuationUri only on the Fabric API host, so the bearer token is never sent elsewhere (#631, #434); shape plugins signatures refuse a RECORD path with a line break, which could make two file lists share one signed message (#579); shape share-bundle verify refuses a data member whose extension is not lower case, which the dataset id did not cover (#683); redact_sensitive removes every value-bearing key of a classified column, not only topk and examples (#394); release_for withholds the joint block when a column is classified above the target, and treats placeholders as values (#650). bandit -r src -ll is clean again: the DDL constraint-name suffix marks its SHA-1 as usedforsecurity=False (names are unchanged).

  • Documentation site (mkdocs.yml, pip install -e ".[docs]", mkdocs build --strict): a navigation over every page in docs/, a home page, a CLI reference generated from the shape parser and a performance page generated from the committed benchmark results (a workload's time is shown only after its equivalence verifier passed). Links to files outside docs/ point at the repository on the site. scripts/check_doc_links.py checks every link in the sources and, with --site, every link and anchor of the built site, offline; scripts/check_user_facing.py --site also scans the built site.

  • Byte-identical files (docs/GENERATION_STABILITY.md, "Byte-identical files"): for the same spec, seed, scale, writer options and Shape version, the CSV, TSV, JSON Lines and SQL (every dialect) writers give identical bytes on Linux, Windows and macOS, in both kernel modes, whatever the locale, time zone, PYTHONHASHSEED or thread count. Fixes: the JSON Lines writer wrote \r\n line ends on Windows (its file was opened without newline="\n"), and so did the _shape_provenance.json sidecar; Linux and macOS bytes are unchanged, and the existing golden writer files and pinned dataset ids are unchanged. The csv, tsv, jsonl and sql sinks declare format_version = 1; the run manifest records the versions it used in reproducibility.writers (additive; the manifest version stays 1); shape.generation.output.writer_format_versions lists them. New shape.repro.file_hashes(run_dir): the SHA-256 of every file a run wrote. The reference pools are frozen by src/shape/builtins/strategies/pools/MANIFEST.json (format: "shape-pool-manifest", version 1; python -m shape.builtins.strategies.pool_manifest [--write]): changing a pool needs the generator version of every strategy that draws from it raised in the same change. The golden byte corpus tests/generation/golden_bytes/ (format: "shape-golden-bytes", version 1; python scripts/golden_bytes.py [--update]) holds the hash of every file written for every built-in strategy, distribution, native provider and column type, checked in both kernel modes and under a non-UTF-8 locale and TZ=Pacific/Chatham. .gitattributes keeps a checkout from changing the line ends of the pools and the corpus.

  • Healthcare code sets (sqllocks-shape-healthcare-codes): two risk-adjustment tables built from the CMS "2027 Initial Model Software" with provenance in the catalog and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md: hcc_hierarchy (model, hcc, drops, in the published order) and hcc_coefficients (model, segment, variable, coefficient kept as the published decimal text, payment_years, software) for CMS-HCC V28 and V22, ESRD V24 and V21 and RxHCC V08 (its three calibrations). shape healthcare-codes fetch hcc_hierarchy hcc_coefficients builds them; byo reads the CMS zip or a delimited file.
